title_en: Georgia judge blocks own order to turn over US election ballot copies to state board
title_zh: 佐治亚州法官阻止自己将美国选举选票副本移交给州委员会的命令
summary: Superior court judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe paused the order after county election officials filed a notice of appeal A judge in Fulton county, Georgia , has blocked her own order to turn over electronic copies of 2020 election ballots seized by the FBI in a raid t
summary_zh: 在县选举官员提交上诉通知后，佐治亚州富尔顿县的一名法官暂停了该命令，高级法院法官凯利·李·埃勒布（Kelly Lee Ellerbe）暂停了该命令。
body_en: Superior court judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe paused the order after county election officials filed a notice of appeal
A judge in Fulton county, Georgia , has blocked her own order to turn over electronic copies of 2020 election ballots seized by the FBI in a raid to the Georgia state election board.

The ballots are at the center of an ongoing dispute over the results of the 2020 election which some Republicans, led by Donald Trump , claimed had been rigged despite Joe Biden being certified after several recounts.
Republican state officials refused to overturn the result, despite a now-infamous phone call from Trump to pressure the Georgia secretary of state, Brad Raffensperger, to “find 11,780 votes”.

Earlier this year, the FBI raided Fulton county’s elections office, seizing 2020 election ballots as part of an investigation into alleged “irregularities”. A federal judge later ruled that the government doesn’t have to return the election ballots after rejecting an argument by the county that the seizure was improper and unconstitutional.
The issue remains a political flashpoint, with Democrats questioning why the former director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, accompanied the FBI on the raid.

Virginia senator Mark Warner, a Democrat, said at a hearing in March he believed Gabbard’s involvement “potentially provide a pretext for the president’s unconstitutional efforts to seize control of the upcoming elections”.

Judge Ellerbe’s protective order said the state election board can use the records for its investigations but says the records cannot be disclosed to anyone other than people identified in the order, which includes the board members and staff, as well as experts they may consult.
body_zh: 在县选举官员提出上诉通知后，高等法院法官凯利·李·埃勒布暂停了该命令
佐治亚州富尔顿县的一名法官阻止了她自己的命令，即向佐治亚州选举委员会移交联邦调查局在突袭中扣押的 2020 年选举选票的电子副本。
这些选票是围绕 2020 年选举结果持续争论的焦点，以唐纳德·特朗普为首的一些共和党人声称，尽管乔·拜登在多次重新计票后获得了认证，但选举结果受到了操纵。
尽管特朗普打电话给佐治亚州国务卿布拉德·拉芬斯佩格（Brad Raffensperger）施压，要求“找到 11,780 票”，但共和党州官员拒绝推翻结果。
今年早些时候，联邦调查局突袭了富尔顿县选举办公室，没收了 2020 年选举选票，作为对所谓“违规行为”调查的一部分。一名联邦法官后来裁定，政府不必归还选举选票，因为该县驳回了该县关于没收选票不适当且违宪的论点。
这个问题仍然是一个政治热点，民主党人质疑为什么前国家情报总监图尔西·加巴德 (Tulsi Gabbard) 陪同联邦调查局 (FBI) 进行突袭。
弗吉尼亚州民主党参议员马克·沃纳 (Mark Warner) 在 3 月份的一次听证会上表示，他认为加巴德的参与“可能为总统为夺取即将举行的选举的控制权而采取违宪行动提供借口”。
埃勒贝法官的保护令称，州选举委员会可以使用这些记录进行调查，但表示这些记录不能透露给命令中指定的人以外的任何人，其中包括委员会成员和工作人员，以及他们可能咨询的专家。

title_en: Trump to visit maker of semiconductor chips, including Nvidia's
title_zh: 特朗普将访问包括英伟达在内的半导体芯片制造商
summary: President Trump will visit the Phoenix TSMC facility, one of the largest manufacturers of advanced chips, including Nvidia's.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统将参观位于菲尼克斯的台积电工厂，该工厂是最大的先进芯片制造商之一，其中包括英伟达的芯片。
body_en: Trump to visit Arizona manufacturer of semiconductor chips, including Nvidia's - CBS News

A White House official said Thursday that President Trump is planning to visit the groundbreaking of a Phoenix facility for a manufacturer of semiconductor chips, including for Nvidia, a trip that comes as the company is under increasing scrutiny for the president's involvement in reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO after he had an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

On Dec. 4, Mr. Trump will tour and deliver remarks at the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company facility in Phoenix, Arizona, a White House official confirmed Thursday. The Taiwan-based company has been expanding in Arizona since 2020, according to the company's website , and next week's visit will be to the latest expansion of its facilities.
A TSMC spokesperson also confirmed to CBS News in a statement that the president was expected to attend the groundbreaking.
The White House official said the new expansion is expected to fund more than 10,000 direct jobs and another 11,000 indirect jobs in the surrounding community.
It's unclear whether Arizona Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs or the state's Democratic Sens. Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego would attend the event next week.

The planned visit comes amid scrutiny of Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, with its high-powered chips emerging as integral to the race for AI dominance between the U.S. and China. Co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang earlier this month resigned after the news broke of his alleged affair with Alice Huang, a former top executive at Singapore-based tech firm Megaspeed and who U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of spying for China . China has denied it.

Mr. Trump advocated for Jensen Huang to be reinstated at Nvidia, with an official saying earlier this week that reinstating him would "preserve America's technological edge over China, strengthen our national security" and ensure the future of AI will be built in the U.S. Sources also told CBS News that Mr. Trump was privately concerned about the broader implications for the U.S. economy should Nvidia's value collapse.
Nvidia's board reinstated Huang on Monday , and Mr. Trump touted his return in a social media post shortly afterward.

一名白宫官员周四表示，特朗普总统计划参观一家包括英伟达在内的半导体芯片制造商在凤凰城的工厂破土动工仪式，此次访问正值该公司因总统参与恢复黄仁勋首席执行官职务而受到越来越多的审查。黄仁勋与一名被指控为中国间谍的女性有染。
一位白宫官员周四证实，12 月 4 日，特朗普将参观位于亚利桑那州凤凰城的台积电工厂并发表讲话。据该公司网站称，这家台湾公司自 2020 年以来一直在亚利桑那州进行扩张，下周将参观其设施的最新扩建。
台积电发言人也在一份声明中向哥伦比亚广播公司新闻证实，预计总统将出席奠基仪式。
白宫官员表示，新的扩建预计将为周边社区提供超过 10,000 个直接就业岗位和另外 11,000 个间接就业岗位。
目前尚不清楚亚利桑那州民主党州长凯蒂·霍布斯或该州民主党参议员马克·凯利和鲁本·加莱戈是否会参加下周的活动。

特朗普主张让黄仁勋恢复在英伟达的职位，一位官员本周早些时候表示，恢复黄仁勋的职位将“维护美国对中国的技术优势，加强我们的国家安全”，并确保人工智能的未来将建立在美国。消息人士还告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，特朗普私下担心如果英伟达的价值崩溃，会对美国经济产生更广泛的影响。

title_en: Trump administration proposes new tariffs on goods from major U.S. trading partners
title_zh: 特朗普政府提议对美国主要贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税
summary: President Trump's new proposed tariffs are already meeting pushback from Democrats and some free trade advocates.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统提出的新关税已经遭到民主党和一些自由贸易倡导者的抵制。
body_en: Trump administration proposes new tariffs on goods from major U.S. trading partners President Trump's new proposed tariffs are already meeting pushback from Democrats and some free trade advocates.
President Trump's new proposed tariffs are already meeting pushback from Democrats and some free trade advocates.

The Trump administration is proposing new tariffs on goods from 14 of the U.S.'s biggest trading partners, including Japan, the EU and China. It's arguing that these new tariffs fight other countries' unfair trade practices, but it's not clear that they will actually do that.
For more, we have NPR White House correspondent Danielle Kurtzleben. Danielle, what did the White House outline yesterday?

DANIELLE KURTZLEBEN, BYLINE: Well, it's new proposed tariffs on goods from major trading partners - the ones you mentioned, and also South Korea and Cambodia, for example. And the rates could go as high as 40% on Chinese goods, also 35% on goods from Vietnam and 20 or 25% on goods from other countries. They're also proposing additional tariffs on sugar and aircrafts from Brazil, and that would add to previous tariffs the U.S. imposed there.
MARTÍNEZ: When could these plans actually become real?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, they could go into effect within a couple of months. That's what U.S. Trade Ambassador Jamieson Greer said yesterday. Now, as for what the rates will be, well, that's still unclear, and that's because for each country, excepting those additional tariffs on Brazil, the White House has two rates they've listed - a proposed rate and a deal rate. To give an example, the tariff on China could be 20%. That's the deal rate. But depending in part on how ongoing discussions go, the rates on Chinese goods could go as high as 40%.
MARTÍNEZ: Forty percent. Now, yeah, the Supreme Court struck down some of Trump's earlier tariffs. So how is the White House legally justifying these new ones?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, these are being implemented under a law known for short as Section 301, which is meant to counter other countries' unfair trade practices. And so here the White House is alleging that these other countries have what's called structural excess capacity in various manufactured goods. And the administration has described this as when another country has policies that cause a good to be overproduced, which then distorts a global market for that good. And so those practices, according to the administration, can include all sorts of things, like labor practices, subsidies and tax breaks.

Now, the administration imposed other sweeping 301 tariffs earlier this year, and there's a lawsuit in process challenging those, with the key argument being that those tariffs were just way broader than the 301 law calls for.
MARTÍNEZ: Now, you mentioned a lawsuit. Could these new tariffs face similar legal challenges?

KURTZLEBEN: You know, they could. We'll see what happens. But I talked to Sara Albrecht. She's chairman and CEO of the nonpartisan Liberty and Justice Center (ph), which filed that lawsuit against those earlier tariffs. And she said these new tariffs are not being used the way 301 tariffs are supposed to.

SARA ALBRECHT: It is a negotiating tactic. That is not what tariffs, in a broad sense, are supposed to be. Like, you can do that on a country-by-country basis if they're addressing a specific problem, not just general, hey, we want better trade deals.

KURTZLEBEN: In addition, both she and other trade experts say they think the White House is just proposing these new tariffs as a way to replace the sweeping tariffs the Supreme Court struck down earlier this year.
MARTÍNEZ: Now, we all just found out how unpopular these tariffs were in the midterm elections. So how are these new tariffs landing politically?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, we've heard some real pushback from congressional Democrats. Richard Neal, top House Democrat on the Ways and Means Committee, said in a statement, quote, "Trump is putting everything from family budgets to our national security at risk to keep his tariff scheme in place."

Now, congressional Republicans have been quieter, and this does come a few weeks after they lost dozens of seats in the election, which is widely attributed, in large part, to high prices, and tariffs do cause higher prices.
body_zh: 特朗普政府提议对美国主要贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税特朗普总统提出的新关税已经遭到民主党和一些自由贸易倡导者的抵制。
特朗普总统提出的新关税已经遭到民主党和一些自由贸易倡导者的抵制。
特朗普政府提议对日本、欧盟和中国等美国 14 个最大贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税。有人认为这些新关税是为了对抗其他国家的不公平贸易行为，但目前尚不清楚他们是否真的会这样做。
如需了解更多信息，请听 NPR 白宫记者 Danielle Kurtzleben 的报道。丹妮尔，白宫昨天概述了什么？
丹尼尔·库兹勒本连线：嗯，这是对主要贸易伙伴——你提到的那些，还有韩国和柬埔寨——的商品征收的新关税。中国商品的税率可能高达 40%，越南商品的税率可能高达 35%，其他国家商品的税率可能高达 20% 或 25%。他们还提议对来自巴西的糖和飞机征收额外关税，这将增加美国之前对巴西征收的关税。
马丁内斯：这些计划什么时候才能真正成为现实？
KURTZLEBEN：嗯，它们可能会在几个月内生效。这是美国贸易大使贾米森·格里尔昨天所说的。现在，至于税率是多少，目前还不清楚，因为对于每个国家来说，除了对巴西的额外关税之外，白宫列出了两种税率——提议税率和交易税率。举个例子，对中国的关税可能是20%。这就是成交率。但部分取决于当前讨论的进展情况，中国商品的关税可能高达 40%。
马丁内斯：百分之四十。现在，是的，最高法院撤销了特朗普早些时候的一些关税。那么白宫如何在法律上证明这些新措施的合理性呢？
KURTZLEBEN：嗯，这些是根据简称为“301 条款”的法律实施的，该法律旨在打击其他国家的不公平贸易行为。因此，白宫在这里声称这些其他国家在各种制成品方面存在所谓的结构性产能过剩。政府将这种情况描述为另一个国家的政策导致某种商品生产过剩，从而扭曲该商品的全球市场。因此，根据政府的说法，这些做法可以包括各种各样的内容，例如劳工做法、补贴和税收减免。
现在，美国政府在今年早些时候征收了其他全面的 301 关税，并且有一项诉讼正在审理中，对这些关税提出质疑，关键论点是这些关税的范围比 301 法律要求的范围要广泛得多。
马丁内斯：现在，你提到了一场诉讼。这些新关税是否会面临类似的法律挑战？
KURTZLEBEN：你知道，他们可以。我们会看看会发生什么。但我和萨拉·阿尔布雷希特谈过。她是无党派自由与正义中心（ph）的董事长兼首席执行官，该中心针对先前的关税提起了诉讼。她表示，这些新关税并未按照 301 关税应有的方式使用。
SARA ALBRECHT：这是一种谈判策略。从广义上讲，这并不是关税应有的样子。就像，如果他们解决的是特定问题，而不仅仅是一般性问题，你可以逐个国家这样做，嘿，我们想要更好的贸易协议。
库兹勒本：此外，她和其他贸易专家都表示，他们认为白宫提出这些新关税只是为了取代最高法院今年早些时候驳回的全面关税。
马丁内斯：现在，我们都刚刚发现这些关税在中期选举中是多么不受欢迎。那么这些新关税如何在政治上落地呢？
库兹勒本：嗯，我们听到了国会民主党人的一些真正的反对意见。众议院筹款委员会首席民主党人理查德·尼尔(Richard Neal)在一份声明中表示，“特朗普为了维持他的关税计划，正在将从家庭预算到我们国家安全的一切都置于危险之中。”
现在，国会共和党人变得更加安静，而且这确实发生在他们在选举中失去数十个席位的几周后，人们普遍将这在很大程度上归因于高价格，而关税确实导致了更高的价格。

title_en: Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., shares why he opposes Trump's proposed tariffs
title_zh: 弗吉尼亚州民主党参议员蒂姆·凯恩分享了他反对特朗普提议的关税的原因
summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine about the Democrat's opposition to President Trump's new tariffs.
summary_zh: NPR 的 A Martinez 与弗吉尼亚州参议员 Tim Kaine 谈论了民主党对特朗普总统新关税的反对。
body_en: Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., shares why he opposes Trump's proposed tariffs NPR's A Martinez speaks with Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine about the Democrat's opposition to President Trump's new tariffs.
NPR's A Martinez speaks with Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine about the Democrat's opposition to President Trump's new tariffs.

All right. Let's go now to one of the lawmakers who's been trying to fight the president's tariffs in Congress. Democratic Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia backed multiple bills meant to curb or refund the administration's tariffs, including legislation that would constrain the president's ability to impose new tariffs at all.
Senator, happy Thanksgiving. Thanks for joining us on Turkey Day.
TIM KAINE: A, very glad to be with you. And our Turkey Day is going to cost about 6% more than it cost last year...
KAINE: ...Partly because of tariffs. So this is a good topic.
MARTÍNEZ: Well, let's get into that. So the president says the objective is to counter unfair foreign trade practices. What's your view of that rationale?

KAINE: Well, in the big picture, what the president has said is this tariff strategy applied everywhere is going to increase manufacturing jobs in the United States. To the contrary, manufacturing jobs in the United States have declined during President Trump's second term. He also said it would reduce our trade deficit. The trade deficit has increased during President Trump's second term. So neither of the goals that he has have been achieved by his tariff strategy. And one of the things he promised to do - bring prices down - has been dramatically affected in the negative way you saw the inflation numbers yesterday. We're seeing dramatic inflation driven by tariffs in the Iran war. So this is an economic strategy that is a big failure.

MARTÍNEZ: You mentioned manufacturing jobs are not happening in the way that we were told they would happen. But how do you square that with the Steelworkers Union who says that the new tariffs are long overdue?

KAINE: There are particular sectors that like them. I mean, the steel industry likes more steel production in the U.S. But overall, if you look at manufacturing, generally, manufacturing jobs are down. They were up during the Biden administration. They're down during the Trump administration with President Trump saying that the tariffs were going to cause this big manufacturing renaissance.

MARTÍNEZ: So I mentioned your efforts in the Senate to fight the president's tariffs. What is your strongest argument for passing legislation to stop the president from imposing these particular tariffs?

KAINE: So there's a broad argument, and then there's kind of a narrow focused one. So here's the broad one. The Constitution gives tariff power to Congress, not the president. And Congresses of both parties, in my view, have made mistakes over decades in handing off this power, delegating it to the president and allowing the president to impose tariffs on his own. Just to allow one person to impose taxes is not a good idea. And so there are a variety of strategies. I - we - I did work with Senator Paul of Kentucky, and we led the effort against the president's use of the IEEPA statute to impose tariffs. The Supreme Court ultimately struck down...
MARTÍNEZ: International Emergency Economic Powers Act, yeah.

KAINE: That's right, yeah. And the Supreme Court ultimately struck down any imposition of tariffs under that statute. But we're looking at the remaining statutes that Congress has sort of handed the power to the president in one of two ways. You can either repeal those statutes and eliminate any presidential ability to impose tariffs. Or recognizing that presidents sometimes need to move quick - quicker than Congress can - you could allow the president to impose tariffs for a limited period of time, say 60 or 90 days, but those tariffs would expire unless Congress affirmatively validates them and continues them.
So those are some of the legal solutions that are on the table. And with Democratic majorities, I think we have a very good chance of getting some of these bills to President Trump's desk.

MARTÍNEZ: You have 56 U.S. senators in - next year. What's the likelihood that you're going to get enough Republicans that share your view? You mentioned Rand Paul, but you're going to need more if you want to pass legislation that the president can't veto.

KAINE: We will. We - my prediction is we're going to get enough Republican votes in the aftermath of the election, which was really a repudiation of tariffs and the war. We'll get enough Republican votes to put tariff bills on President Trump's desk. Now, here comes the next challenge. If he vetoes those bills, would we have enough to have a two-thirds vote in both Houses to override his veto? That's a - more of an uphill climb. But we're going to test that. We're going to put bills on his desk, dramatically limiting his tariff powers to try to help Americans' pocketbooks. And then we'll say to him, if you veto this bill, you're just going to hurt people. So why don't you just sign it?

参议员，感恩节快乐。感谢您在火鸡日加入我们。
蒂姆·凯恩：A，很高兴和你在一起。我们的火鸡节费用将比去年增加约 6%...
凯恩：……部分是因为关税。所以这是一个很好的话题。
马丁内斯：好吧，让我们开始吧。因此总统表示，目标是打击不公平的外贸行为。您对此理由有何看法？

凯恩：嗯，从大局来看，总统所说的是，这种在各地实施的关税策略将增加美国的制造业就业机会。相反，在特朗普总统第二任期内，美国制造业就业岗位有所下降。他还表示，这将减少我们的贸易逆差。特朗普总统第二任期内贸易逆差有所增加。因此，他的关税策略并没有实现他的这两个目标。他承诺要做的事情之一——降低物价——已经受到了巨大的负面影响，正如你昨天看到的通胀数据一样。我们看到伊朗战争中的关税导致了剧烈的通货膨胀。所以这是一个巨大失败的经济战略。
马丁内斯：您提到制造业工作并没有像我们被告知的那样发生。但您如何看待钢铁工人工会表示新关税早就应该征收的说法呢？
凯恩：有一些特定的部门喜欢它们。我的意思是，钢铁行业希望美国增加钢铁产量。但总的来说，如果你看看制造业，制造业的就业机会普遍下降。他们在拜登执政期间崛起。在特朗普执政期间，这些数字有所下降，特朗普总统表示，关税将带来制造业的大规模复兴。
马丁内斯：所以我提到了你们在参议院为对抗总统关税所做的努力。您认为通过立法阻止总统征收这些特定关税的最有力论据是什么？
凯恩：所以有一个广泛的争论，然后有一个狭隘的焦点争论。这是广义的。宪法将关税权力赋予国会，而不是总统。在我看来，几十年来，两党国会在将这一权力移交给总统并允许总统自行征收关税方面都犯了错误。仅仅让一个人征税并不是一个好主意。所以有各种各样的策略。我——我们——我确实与肯塔基州参议员保罗合作，我们领导了反对总统利用 IEEPA 法规征收关税的努力。最终最高法院驳回了...
马丁内斯：《国际紧急经济权力法》，是的。
凯恩：没错，是的。最高法院最终否决了根据该法规征收的任何关税。但我们正在研究国会通过以下两种方式之一将权力移交给总统的剩余法规。您可以废除这些法规并消除总统征收关税的任何权力。或者认识到总统有时需要迅速采取行动——比国会更快——你可以允许总统在有限的时间内征收关税，比如 60 或 90 天，但这些关税将到期，除非国会确认并继续实施。
这些是摆在桌面上的一些法律解决方案。由于民主党占多数，我认为我们很有可能将其中一些法案提交给特朗普总统。
马丁内斯：明年将有 56 名美国参议员。你获得足够多的共和党人同意你的观点的可能性有多大？你提到了兰德·保罗，但如果你想通过总统无法否决的立法，你将需要更多。

凯恩：我们会的。我们 - 我的预测是，我们将在选举后获得足够的共和党选票，这实际上是对关税和战争的否定。我们将获得足够的共和党选票，将关税法案放到特朗普总统的办公桌上。现在，下一个挑战来了。如果他否决这些法案，我们是否有足够的票数在参众两院获得三分之二的票数来推翻他的否决？这更像是一次艰难的攀登。但我们要测试一下。我们将把账单放在他的办公桌上，极大地限制他试图帮助美国人改善钱包的关税权力。然后我们会对他说，如果你否决这项法案，你只会伤害人们。那你为什么不直接签字呢？

title_en: Trump claims "fake economic numbers" were released before election
title_zh: 特朗普声称大选前发布了“虚假经济数据”
summary: President Trump demanded an investigation into the Commerce Department's recent revising of the GDP, which happens routinely.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统要求对商务部最近对 GDP 的修改进行调查，这种情况很常见。
body_en: Trump spends Thanksgiving at golf club, accuses Commerce Department of releasing "fake economic numbers" - CBS News
President Trump is spending Thanksgiving in Florida, where he had a policy meeting early Thursday morning and then headed to his golf club nearby.

He and first lady Melania Trump, who are staying at Mar-a-Lago, called U.S. service members on Thursday evening, including members of a unit that was involved in Operation Epic Fury, saying Iran "will never have a nuclear weapon."

On Thursday morning, Mr. Trump posted a holiday message on social media, wishing a happy Thanksgiving to the "American patriots who have worked so hard to make our country great!" He continued in the lengthy post to wish a happy Thanksgiving to several others with whom he has grievances, including the Commerce Department, immigrants, "the radical far left" and more.

Mr. Trump claimed that before the midterm elections where Republicans suffered heavy losses , there were "fake Economic Numbers" released. Mr. Trump cited the Commerce Department on Wednesday revising the gross domestic product in the third quarter to 4.3% on an annual basis, up from a prior estimate of 3.4%. The Commerce Department regularly updates its monthly economic data to improve its accuracy, including not just the GDP but also the monthly employment data.
Although he did not present any evidence, the president demanded an investigation.

Mr. Trump also wished a happy holiday to "all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left, those that are looking to change our Court System to that of Sharia, those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work."
The president continued his post with messages about the Somali community, deported immigrants and those who he believes do not appreciate the White House ballroom he is constructing.

Overnight, Mr. Trump praised the Army's controlled detonation of about five tons of degraded lead azide in Iowa, blaming former President Barack Obama for the situation and writing that no "carcinogens were released into beautiful Iowa air." Although Mr. Trump and other administration officials have praised the detonation, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News on Wednesday that prior to it, there was a chaotic lead-up inside the Trump administration about what went wrong and who was to blame for not elevating the matter to senior officials sooner.

On Wednesday night, Mr. Trump met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, and the pair issued a joint statement describing the meeting as "very impactful" and focused on Russia, Ukraine and Iran. The statement said they discussed "the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war."

Mr. Trump earlier in the week continued the annual tradition of pardoning turkeys, sending turkeys named Freedom and Feathers to live on a farm in Texas. Melania Trump, meanwhile, welcomed the official White House Christmas tree on Monday.

特朗普总统正在佛罗里达州度过感恩节，周四早上他在那里举行了一次政策会议，然后前往附近的高尔夫俱乐部。
他和住在海湖庄园的第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普周四晚上给美国军人打电话，其中包括参与史诗愤怒行动的部队成员，称伊朗“永远不会拥有核武器”。
周四上午，特朗普在社交媒体上发布节日致辞，祝“为让我们的国家伟大而辛勤工作的美国爱国者们感恩节快乐！”他在这篇长文中继续祝愿其他几个与他有恩怨的人感恩节快乐，其中包括商务部、移民、“激进极左派”等。
特朗普声称，在共和党遭受重大损失的中期选举之前，发布了“虚假经济数据”。特朗普周三援引商务部的话说，将第三季度国内生产总值按年率修正为 4.3%，高于此前估计的 3.4%。商务部定期更新月度经济数据以提高准确性，不仅包括GDP，还包括月度就业数据。
尽管他没有提供任何证据，但总统要求进行调查。
特朗普先生还祝愿“所有那些为将我们的国家推向激进极左而辛勤工作的人，那些希望将我们的法院系统改为伊斯兰教法的人，那些想要重新分配财产的人，以便所有辛勤工作的人们在一生中积累了一定的财富，现在将被迫在全国各地分配它，甚至是那些拒绝工作的人。”
总统继续发表有关索马里社区、被驱逐移民和他认为不欣赏他正在建造的白宫宴会厅的人的信息。
一夜之间，特朗普称赞陆军在爱荷华州控制引爆了约五吨降解的叠氮化铅，将这种情况归咎于前总统巴拉克·奥巴马，并写道“没有任何致癌物质释放到爱荷华州美丽的空气中”。尽管特朗普和其他政府官员对这次爆炸表示赞赏，但知情人士周三告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，在此之前，特朗普政府内部对于出了什么问题以及谁应该为没有尽早向高级官员报告此事负责而进行了混乱的讨论。
周三晚上，特朗普会见了北约秘书长马克·吕特，两人发表了一份联合声明，称这次会议“非常有影响力”，重点关注俄罗斯、乌克兰和伊朗。声明称，他们讨论了“俄罗斯避免采取任何有意或无意扩大战争的行动的重要性”。
本周早些时候，特朗普延续了一年一度的赦免火鸡的传统，将名为“自由”和“羽毛”的火鸡送到德克萨斯州的一个农场生活。与此同时，梅拉尼娅·特朗普周一欢迎白宫官方圣诞树。

title_en: Trump alleges ‘fake’ economic figures released before US midterms but doesn’t provide evidence
title_zh: 特朗普声称美国中期选举前公布的经济数据“虚假”，但没有提供证据
summary: In a Thanksgiving post, the US president seeks investigation after blue wave of Democrats unseat Republicans Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake
summary_zh: 在感恩节帖子中，唐纳德·特朗普在没有证据的情况下声称民主党的蓝色浪潮取代了共和党，美国总统寻求调查
body_en: Trump alleges ‘fake’ economic figures released before US midterms but doesn’t provide evidence | Donald Trump
In a Thanksgiving post, the US president seeks investigation after blue wave of Democrats unseat Republicans

Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party.

In a holiday message on social media tinged with bitterness, the US president wished a happy thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”.

While revisions to official economic figures are commonplace, Trump has tried time and again to challenge trust in economic data that does not support his claims that a historic boom is underway in the US.
The US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), an agency within the US Department of Commerce, calculates gross domestic product, or GDP, numbers.

“Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Thursday. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error”.

Trump has repeatedly claimed since taking office in January 2025 that an economic “golden age” is taking hold on his watch. Many Americans have been grappling with a higher cost of living, however – exacerbated by the economic fallout of his war on Iran – and backed Democrats in the midterms.

Trump continued his acerbic well-wishing for “a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left” as well as “those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work”.

And he revisited another ongoing beef with the news media over his controversial focus on White House renovations and decorations. “I want to commiserate with those reporters and citizens who don’t understand filth, dirt, lack of maintenance, and corruption, and are upset with me because I took time out of my very busy schedule to fix the 17 broken windows, numerous chipped and decaying columns, broken, dilapidated, and missing moldings, and lack of a proper plaster and paint job on the White House.”
The sarcastic intervention continued with a message of thanks to “the murderers, drug dealers, and criminals of all shapes, sizes, and colors” whom he claimed are “mostly gone now”.

“Happy Thanksgiving to them anyway, even though from faraway lands,” he concluded. “We miss you dearly, but you will never be back, and America will never allow what you have done to us to happen again!”

Democratic senator Chuck Schumer, vying to be majority leader in the chamber following his party’s victories in this month’s election took a more conventional approach , wishing “everyone in New York and across America a joyous and restful Thanksgiving holiday with your friends and family”.

Hakeem Jeffries, whom Democrats have nominated to be the first Black speaker in the House of Representatives, also played it straight. “Happy Thanksgiving to everyone in the community and throughout our great country! Grateful for the civil servants on the job who are working through the stormy weather to keep everyone safe,” he posted on X. “May God bless you all.”
body_zh: 特朗普声称美国中期选举前发布了“虚假”经济数据，但没有提供证据唐纳德·特朗普
在感恩节帖子中，美国总统在民主党蓝色浪潮取代共和党后寻求调查
唐纳德·特朗普在没有证据的情况下声称美国联邦政府在本月中期选举前公布的经济数据是“假的”，并在选民全面拒绝他的共和党后要求进行调查。
在社交媒体上的一则充满苦涩的节日信息中，美国总统祝愿感恩节快乐，“即使是那些在选举前发布虚假经济数据的人，并在三周后的昨天修正了这些数据，显示GDP实际上是4.3%，而不是3.4%”。
虽然官方经济数据的修改很常见，但特朗普一次又一次地试图挑战人们对经济数据的信任，这些数据并不支持他关于美国正在经历历史性繁荣的说法。
美国经济分析局 (BEA) 是美国商务部的一个机构，负责计算国内生产总值 (GDP) 数据。
“为什么在选举前没有发布正确的数字？我要求立即对这一情况进行调查，”特朗普周四在他的真相社交平台上写道。 “这不是一个小错误，这是一个巨大的、有目的的错误”。
特朗普自 2025 年 1 月上任以来多次声称，经济“黄金时代”正在他的任期内到来。然而，许多美国人一直在努力应对生活成本上升的问题 — — 由于他对伊朗的战争造成的经济影响而加剧 — — 并在中期选举中支持民主党。
特朗普继续尖刻地祝愿“所有那些辛勤工作把我们的国家带向激进极左的人们”以及“那些想要重新分配财产的人们，感恩节快乐，这样所有辛勤工作的人们在一生中积累了一定的财富，现在将被迫在全国各地分配，甚至是那些拒绝工作的人”。
他还重新审视了另一起因他对白宫翻修和装饰的争议焦点而与新闻媒体发生的争执。 “我想向那些不了解肮脏、肮脏、缺乏维护和腐败的记者和公民表示同情，他们对我感到不安，因为我在非常繁忙的日程中抽出时间来修复白宫的 17 扇破损的窗户、无数破损和腐烂的柱子、破损、破旧和缺失的装饰线条，以及缺乏适当的灰泥和油漆工作。”
讽刺性的干预继续进行，并向“凶手、毒贩和各种形状、大小和肤色的罪犯”表示感谢，他声称这些人“现在大部分已经消失了”。
“无论如何，祝他们感恩节快乐，即使他们来自遥远的地方，”他总结道。 “我们非常想念你，但你永远不会回来，美国永远不会允许你对我们所做的事情再次发生！”
民主党参议员查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)在其政党在本月的选举中获胜后，争夺众议院多数党领袖的地位，采取了更为传统的方式，祝愿“纽约和全美各地的每个人与朋友和家人度过一个欢乐而宁静的感恩节假期”。
民主党提名的第一位黑人众议院议长哈基姆·杰弗里斯（Hakeem Jeffries）也直言不讳。他在 X 上发帖称：“祝社区和整个伟大国家的每个人感恩节快乐！感谢在暴风雨天气中工作的公务员，确保每个人的安全。愿上帝保佑你们所有人。”

body_en: US Senate ‘permitting bill’ threatens clean water protections to speed up energy projects | US politics
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act passed the Senate and is now being debated in the House

An industry-backed “permitting bill” approved by the US Senate would gut key clean water protections with changes that would do little to speed up the development of major energy projects, advocates warn.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (Baaja) passed the Senate 62-33 and is now being debated in the House. The Baaja is a “permitting reform” bill that aims to reduce the time it takes federal agencies to approve major energy and infrastructure projects, like power lines, fossil fuel pipelines, natural gas plants and datacenters .

But the legislation also includes provisions that would make it more difficult for states to put in place protections against water pollution, double the amount of time between automatic reviews of water pollution permits, and reduce transparency around the types and levels of water pollution.

More than 50 groups in communities impacted by Pfas “forever chemical” water pollution have come out against the bill , warning that they would suffer further if the legislation is approved because it would weaken some of the few mechanisms in US law that regulate the chemicals’ discharge. The law would “put us in more danger”, said Emily Donovan, co-founder of the Clean Cape Fear advocacy group in Wilmington, North Carolina, where drinking, surface, and ground water is polluted by discharge from a nearby Pfas factory .
“We already see how hard it is for the [Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)] to [regulate] Pfas ,” Donovan said. “What frustrates us is we don’t need to make it harder.”

Baaja has drawn wide industry support , including among trade groups like the American Chemistry Council and American Petroleum Institute . It is opposed by virtually every major US environmental group because it would eliminate some foundational environmental protections.

The bill’s supporters say the cost is worth it because it will allow energy projects to be built faster, and hasten the transition to clean energy. Opponents say industry is using the need to transition to clean energy as cover to ram through a range of unnecessary changes to water laws that do nothing to improve energy permitting.

“BAAJA is a handout to the oil and gas industry, while doing very little to solve the permitting problems being used to justify those changes,” the Clean Water Action advocacy group, which is lobbying against the law, said in a statement. “Congress is trading away protections for states, tribes, wetlands and streams even though those protections are largely unrelated to the years-long delays at the center of the permitting debate.”

Among other changes, the bill would allow industry to sue to undo the EPA’s guidance for states on water pollution discharge. The EPA currently develops criteria that states use to limit discharge into waterways. The agency does this without issuing a formal rule, and the criteria cannot easily be challenged in court.

The Baaja would require a formal rule-making process, which would slow the clean water criteria issuance by several years, and open it to lawsuits. The criteria are used by states to develop limits on Pfas water pollution, and the change would shift more responsibility onto states that are largely under-resourced and unable to meet the challenge, Donovan said.

Another provision would change the EPA’s mandatory review of water pollution permits from five years to 10 years. The EPA uses this review mechanism to require polluters to track their Pfas and other water pollution.

Donovan pointed to the Pfas pollution in North Carolina to highlight how the provision would prolong the public’s exposure to dangerous chemicals. North Carolina regulators in 2019 put in place a health advisory limit of 140 parts per tn (ppt) for GenX, one of the main Pfas compounds polluting the state’s waterways. By 2022, the EPA established a health advisory of 10 ppt.

Advocates fear that the extended review period for pollution permits from five to ten years would create a scenario in which a company issued a water permit in 2020 may continue to pollute at higher levels for much longer.

“Imagine not being able to make a change for 10 years despite that the science is showing that a chemical is more toxic than originally thought – that’s what terrifies and frustrates us,” Donovan said. The transition to clean energy does not need to sacrifice clean water, she added.
“We can get clean energy without having to cause cancer,” Donovan said.

两党共同通过的《美国负担能力和就业法案》已在参议院获得通过，目前正在众议院进行辩论
支持者警告说，美国参议院批准的一项得到行业支持的“许可法案”将破坏关键的清洁水保护，其变化对加快重大能源项目的发展几乎无济于事。
两党共同制定的 2026 年美国负担能力和就业法案 (Baaja) 在参议院以 62 比 33 获得通过，目前正在众议院进行辩论。 Baaja 是一项“许可改革”法案，旨在减少联邦机构批准重大能源和基础设施项目（如输电线、化石燃料管道、天然气厂和数据中心）所需的时间。
但该立法还包括一些条款，这些条款将使各州更难实施水污染保护措施，使水污染许可证自动审查之间的时间加倍，并降低水污染类型和水平的透明度。
受 Pfas“永久化学”水污染影响的社区中的 50 多个团体已站出来反对该法案，并警告称，如果该法案获得批准，他们将遭受进一步的损失，因为这将削弱美国法律中少数几个监管化学品排放的机制。北卡罗来纳州威尔明顿清洁开普恐惧倡导组织的联合创始人艾米丽·多诺万表示，这项法律将“让我们陷入更大的危险”，那里的饮用水、地表水和地下水均因附近一家 Pfas 工厂的排放而受到污染。
“我们已经看到 [环境保护局 (EPA)] [监管] Pfa 有多么困难，”多诺万说。 “令我们沮丧的是我们不需要让事情变得更难。”
Baaja 得到了广泛的行业支持，包括美国化学理事会和美国石油协会等贸易团体的支持。它几乎遭到美国所有主要环保组织的反对，因为它将消除一些基本的环境保护措施。
该法案的支持者表示，这笔成本是值得的，因为它将使能源项目建设更快，并加速向清洁能源的过渡。反对者表示，工业界正在利用向清洁能源过渡的需要作为掩护，强行对水法进行一系列不必要的修改，而这些修改对改善能源许可毫无帮助。
正在游说反对这项法律的清洁水行动倡导组织在一份声明中表示，“BAAJA 是对石油和天然气行业的一份施舍，但几乎没有解决用于证明这些变化合理性的许可问题。” “国会正在放弃对州、部落、湿地和溪流的保护，尽管这些保护在很大程度上与许可辩论中心长达数年的拖延无关。”
除其他变化外，该法案将允许工业界提起诉讼，以撤销美国环保局对各州水污染排放的指导。美国环保署目前制定了各州用于限制向水道排放的标准。该机构在没有发布正式规则的情况下做到了这一点，而且这些标准不能轻易在法庭上受到质疑。
Baaja 将需要一个正式的规则制定程序，这将使清洁水标准的发布速度推迟数年，并导致诉讼。多诺万说，各州使用这些标准来制定对 Pfas 水污染的限制，这一变化将把更多的责任转移到资源严重不足且无法应对挑战的各州身上。
另一项规定将把 EPA 对水污染许可证的强制审查从五年改为 10 年。 EPA 使用这种审查机制要求污染者追踪其 Pfa 和其他水污染。
多诺万指出北卡罗来纳州的 Pfas 污染，强调该规定将如何延长公众接触危险化学品的时间。北卡罗来纳州监管机构于 2019 年对 GenX 制定了每吨 140 份 (ppt) 的健康建议限值，GenX 是污染该州水道的主要 Pfas 化合物之一。到 2022 年，EPA 制定了 10 ppt 的健康建议。
支持者担心，将污染许可证的审查期限从五年延长到十年，会造成这样一种情况：2020 年颁发取水许可证的公司可能会在更长的时间内继续以更高的水平进行污染。
“想象一下，尽管科学表明某种化学物质的毒性比最初想象的要大，但 10 年内都无法做出改变，这就是让我们感到恐惧和沮丧的原因，”多诺万说。她补充说，向清洁能源的过渡不需要牺牲清洁水。
“我们可以获得清洁能源，而不会导致癌症，”多诺万说。

title_en: Trump calls the pre-election GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of Commerce Department
title_zh: 特朗普称选前GDP数据“虚假”并要求商务部进行调查
summary: President Donald Trump is suggesting without evidence a conspiracy within the government to report upwardly revised economic growth figures after the midterm elections that were disastrous for Republicans
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统在没有证据的情况下暗示政府内部存在阴谋，在经济增长数据公布后上调了经济增长数据。
body_en: President Donald Trump is suggesting without evidence a conspiracy within the government to report upwardly revised economic growth figures after the midterm elections that were disastrous for Republicans

WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. -- President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections, and said he wants to launch an investigation.

Trump has repeatedly sought to undermine trust in economic data that fails to match his claims of a historic boom, a pattern that threatens the credibility of figures needed by businesses, financial markets and consumers when making investments.

His latest complaint concerns data issued by the Commerce Department on Wednesday that revised gross domestic product in the third quarter to 4.3% on an annual basis, up from a prior estimate of 3.4%.

The department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis routinely updates its economic data to improve their accuracy. GDP figures, monthly jobs reports and other data are regularly revised. Those updates occur on a pre-scheduled basis without regard to the political calendar.

But the president claimed on social media that it was a “massive, and purposeful, error” and linked it to the poor performance for Republicans in the Nov. 3 midterm elections that gave Democrats control of both houses of Congress.

“It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE, and a correction was issued yesterday by the people in the Government Agency that does these numbers,” Trump posted. “Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation.”

The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The government is largely closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

It’s the latest instance of Trump questioning the integrity of economic data he feels is unfavorable to him without providing evidence that revisions are politically motivated. In August 2025, Trump fired the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a decidedly weak jobs report. That report said only 73,000 jobs were added in July 2025 and showed that 258,000 fewer jobs were added in May and June than previously reported.
Trump called that jobs report “phony” and “rigged.”

Trump has claimed that he deserves credit for powering stronger economic growth, but voters do not share the president's belief that the economy is strong. In the midterms, 76% described economic conditions as “not so good” or “poor,” according to the AP Voter Poll, an extensive survey of the electorate. About two-thirds of voters said Trump’s own policies had fueled inflation.

The president in his social media post ignored that the same federal agency on Wednesday also reported that a key measure of inflation — the personal consumption expenditures price index — accelerated to an annual pace of 3.8% in October.
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统在没有证据的情况下暗示政府内部存在阴谋，在中期选举后上调经济增长数据，这对共和党来说是灾难性的
佛罗里达州西棕榈滩——唐纳德·特朗普总统周四指责商务部在中期选举前故意发布不正确的经济增长数据，并表示他希望展开调查。
特朗普一再试图破坏人们对经济数据的信任，这些数据与他所声称的历史性繁荣不符，这种模式威胁到企业、金融市场和消费者在投资时所需数据的可信度。
他最新的投诉涉及商务部周三发布的数据，该数据将第三季度国内生产总值按年率修正为 4.3%，高于之前估计的 3.4%。
该部门的经济分析局定期更新其经济数据以提高其准确性。 GDP数据、月度就业报告和其他数据会定期修订。这些更新是按照预先安排的方式进行的，与政治日历无关。
但总统在社交媒体上声称这是一个“巨大的、有目的的错误”，并将其与共和党在 11 月 3 日中期选举中的糟糕表现联系起来，这次中期选举让民主党控制了国会参众两院。
特朗普发帖称：“刚刚透露，选举前公布的真实经济数据是假的，负责这些数据的政府机构的人员昨天发布了更正。” “为什么在选举前没有发布正确的号码？我要求立即调查这一情况。”

商务部没有立即回应置评请求。周四感恩节假期，政府基本关闭。
这是特朗普质疑他认为对他不利的经济数据完整性的最新实例，但没有提供证据表明修改是出于政治动机。 2025 年 8 月，特朗普在就业报告明显疲软后解雇了劳工统计局局长。该报告称，2025 年 7 月仅新增 73,000 个就业岗位，并显示 5 月和 6 月新增就业岗位比之前报告的少 258,000 个。
特朗普称这份就业报告“虚假”且“被操纵”。
特朗普声称，他因推动更强劲的经济增长而值得赞扬，但选民并不认同总统认为经济强劲的信念。根据美联社选民民意调查（对选民进行的一项广泛调查），在中期选举中，76％的人将经济状况描述为“不太好”或“很差”。大约三分之二的选民表示，特朗普自己的政策加剧了通货膨胀。
总统在社交媒体帖子中忽略了同一联邦机构周三还报告称，通胀的一个关键指标——个人消费支出价格指数——10月份年增长率加速至3.8%。

title_en: Kilmar Ábrego García, target of Trump’s immigration crackdown, lands in Spain after ‘leaving happy’
title_zh: 特朗普移民镇压目标基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚在“快乐离开”后抵达西班牙
summary: Ábrego García chooses to depart from US after previously being deported to El Salvador due to ‘administrative error’ Kilmar Ábrego García, the Salvadorian national whose mistaken deportation turned him into a symbol of Donald Trump’s mass deportation efforts,
summary_zh: 阿尔布雷戈·加西亚（Ábrego García）因“行政错误”而被驱逐到萨尔瓦多，之后选择离开美国 Kilmar Ábrego García，萨尔瓦多
body_en: Ábrego García chooses to depart from US after previously being deported to El Salvador due to ‘administrative error’
Kilmar Ábrego García, the Salvadorian national whose mistaken deportation turned him into a symbol of Donald Trump’s mass deportation efforts, has landed in Spain.
Ábrego García arrived in Madrid on Wednesday after leaving the United States of his own volition .

“I feel free of everything evil that has followed me up until this point,” he told reporters on a video call just hours after he touched down. “I’m happy … because this time I’m leaving with my freedom, not like before when they took me out inhumanely.”
He added: “The government does not decide where my story continues. My family and I will decide our future.”
Prior to his departure, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents met him at the airport and removed his ankle monitor, according to We Are Casa, a Maryland-based advocacy group.
As he made his way through the Madrid airport, Ábrego García did not speak to reporters, instead raising his fist in the air as he climbed into a waiting van.
Ábrego García became a lightning rod in the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown in 2025 after he was deported to El Salvador in what an official later called an “administrative error”.

The 31-year-old had been living in the US since 2019, after a judge ruled that he could not be deported to El Salvador due to the dangers posed by a gang that had threatened his family. The judge allowed him to live and work in the US under ICE supervision, but he was not given residency status.

Married to an American woman, the Maryland resident was part of a group of more than 200 people sent by the US to Cecot, a notorious anti-terrorism mega-prison , in violation of the US immigration judge’s 2019 order.

Amid public outcry, he was returned to the US after a decision by the supreme court. Since then, Ábrego García has been fighting government efforts to deport him for a second time to a series of African countries proposed by Department of Homeland Security officials.
On Wednesday, his lawyer, Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, said the Trump administration had wanted to deport Ábrego García “handcuffed, on an ICE flight bound for Liberia” on Tuesday.

“And what happened? He walked out a free man, without any restrictions, without shackles on his feet. He left for the country of his choosing, and he did so on a commercial flight, alongside everyone else,” Sandoval-Moshenberg added.
He described it as a “complete victory”, adding: “Instead of flying ICE Air, he flew United Airlines. Instead of being in shackles, he was in economy plus.”

He said Ábrego García had negotiated a deal with federal authorities in which they had agreed to allow him to leave the country, removing obstacles such as the ankle monitor and taking him off the no-fly list, as long as he left by 24 November. The Department of Homeland Security said on Tuesday Ábrego García had “self-deported” to Spain .

Sandoval-Moshenberg described Ábrego García’s departure from the US as temporary, saying that he would decide where to settle for the next two years as he waited out the remainder of the Trump administration.

“Mr Ábrego García has many options to return to the United States as the husband of a US citizen spouse and the father of a US citizen child,” he said. “We don’t expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritise reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland.”

On Wednesday, Ábrego García’s lawyer, Chris Newman, said his client had landed in Spain as a tourist and that he had no plans to meet with any politicians while in Spain. “I can confirm that he’s coming here with the intention of staying for just a few days and that he already has tickets, one could say, for his next appointment,” he told Spanish media.
His departure this week was celebrated by many who had sought to push back against the Trump administration’s pursuit of Ábrego García.
body_zh: 阿布雷戈·加西亚（Ábrego García）因“行政错误”被驱逐到萨尔瓦多后选择离开美国
萨尔瓦多国民基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Kilmar Ábrego García) 已抵达西班牙，他的错误驱逐使他成为唐纳德·特朗普大规模驱逐行动的象征。
阿布雷戈·加西亚在自愿离开美国后于周三抵达马德里。
“我感觉自己已经摆脱了迄今为止一直伴随着我的一切邪恶，”他在着陆几小时后在视频通话中对记者说。 “我很高兴……因为这次我带着自由离开，而不是像以前那样不人道地把我带走。”
他补充道：“政府不能决定我的故事在哪里继续。我和我的家人将决定我们的未来。”
据马里兰州倡导组织 We Are Casa 称，在他出发之前，移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 特工在机场迎接了他，并取下了他的脚踝监视器。
当阿布雷戈·加西亚穿过马德里机场时，他没有对记者讲话，而是在爬上一辆等候的面包车时举起拳头。
阿夫雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García) 被驱逐到萨尔瓦多，后来一名官员称这是“行政错误”，他因此成为特朗普政府 2025 年移民镇压的避雷针。
这位 31 岁的男子自 2019 年以来一直居住在美国，此前一名法官裁定，由于一个威胁他家人的团伙构成的危险，他不能被驱逐到萨尔瓦多。法官允许他在 ICE 的监督下在美国生活和工作，但没有给予他居留身份。
这位马里兰州居民与一名美国妇女结婚，是美国违反美国移民法官 2019 年的命令，将 200 多人送往臭名昭著的反恐巨型监狱塞科特 (Cecot) 的一员之一。
在公众的强烈抗议下，最高法院做出裁决后，他被遣返美国。从那时起，阿布雷戈·加西亚一直在反对政府根据国土安全部官员的提议第二次将他驱逐到一系列非洲国家的努力。
周三，他的律师西蒙·桑多瓦尔-莫申伯格 (Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg) 表示，特朗普政府希望周二将阿布雷戈·加西亚“戴上手铐，乘坐飞往利比里亚的 ICE 航班”驱逐出境。
“发生了什么事？他以自由人的身份走出去，没有任何限制，脚上没有镣铐。他前往他选择的国家，并与其他人一起乘坐商业航班，”桑多瓦尔-莫申伯格补充道。
他形容这是一次“彻底的胜利”，并补充道：“他没有乘坐ICE航空，而是乘坐联合航空。他没有受到束缚，而是乘坐了经济舱。”
他说，阿布雷戈·加西亚已与联邦当局谈判达成一项协议，同意允许他离开该国，取消脚踝监视器等障碍，并将他从禁飞名单上删除，只要他在 11 月 24 日之前离开即可。美国国土安全部周二表示，阿布雷戈·加西亚已“自行驱逐”至西班牙。
桑多瓦尔-莫申伯格称阿布雷戈·加西亚离开美国是暂时的，并表示他将在等待特朗普政府剩余任期的同时决定未来两年的定居地点。
“作为美国公民配偶的丈夫和美国公民孩子的父亲，阿布雷戈·加西亚先生有多种选择返回美国，”他说。 “我们预计这不会在本届政府领导下发生，我们知道这永远不会给他带来公平的待遇，但我们预计下一届政府将优先考虑让这个家庭团聚并将他带回马里兰州。”
周三，阿布雷戈·加西亚的律师克里斯·纽曼表示，他的当事人以游客身份抵达西班牙，他没有计划在西班牙期间会见任何政客。他告诉西班牙媒体：“我可以证实，他来这里只是打算待几天，而且他已经有了下一次约会的门票。”
许多曾试图阻止特朗普政府追捕阿夫雷戈·加西亚的人本周庆祝了他的离职。

title_en: Court lets Puerto Rico governor fire firm that runs the island's troubled power grid
title_zh: 法院允许波多黎各州长解雇经营该岛陷入困境的电网的公司
summary: LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago. The court's ruling nullifies its contract, and gives the government a year to find a new operator.
summary_zh: 五年前，LUMA Energy 接管了电网。法院裁决其合同无效，并给政府一年时间寻找新歌剧
body_en: Court lets Puerto Rico governor fire firm that runs the island's troubled power grid LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago. The court's ruling nullifies its contract, and gives the government a year to find a new operator.
Puerto Rico Supreme Court allows governor to fire company that runs the island's troubled power grid
LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago. The court's ruling nullifies its contract, and gives the government a year to find a new operator.

Puerto Rico's supreme court has ruled the island's governor can kick out the private company that's been running its troubled power grid for five years. The decision could have huge consequences for electric service in Puerto Rico. Here is NPR's Adrian Florido.

ADRIAN FLORIDO, BYLINE: After Hurricane Maria flattened Puerto Rico's already rickety power grid in 2017, the island's government privatized it. It gave a company called LUMA Energy, based in Canada and Texas, a 15-year deal to take over the power lines, promising that LUMA would rebuild the grid stronger and improve the notoriously unreliable service. LUMA took over in 2021. But things have not gone as planned.

Blackouts are still a constant fact of life. LUMA has come in for harsh criticism from customers and officials. Last year, Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez-Colon filed suit to nullify LUMA's contract. Yesterday, the Puerto Rican Supreme Court ruled in her favor that LUMA must go.
JENNIFFER GONZALEZ-COLON: Today is a day of celebration on the island.
FLORIDO: This is the governor speaking after the ruling. She said LUMA has not lived up to its promises.
GONZALEZ-COLON: More outages on the island, more shutdowns on the island. They have not fulfilled the requirements of the contract.

FLORIDO: In fact, the island's supreme court ruled on procedural grounds, saying officials had not followed local requirements when approving agreements with the company. The court gave the local government a year to put a new operator in place. The governor said the work to find a new private company will start immediately.

GONZALEZ-COLON: It's going to be a good transition. We're going to make it in a year. And I hope that all companies that are interested in participating in this process will fulfill and follow the process of law. And we're going to be opening that process for public bid.

FLORIDO: The court gave LUMA Energy 10 days to request a reconsideration of its ruling. In a statement, LUMA said it is considering its legal options. The company has long argued that the grid it took over was in awful shape and that it is not fully to blame for the blackouts. A new operator will need approval from both the local government and a federal oversight board that Congress put in place 10 years ago to get Puerto Rico out of bankruptcy. In a statement, that board criticized the governor for ending LUMA' s contract without having a new company ready to go. It said it's worried about the continuity of service on the island. In her remarks yesterday, the governor said she has a plan in place and will reveal it soon.

波多黎各最高法院允许州长解雇经营该岛陷入困境的电网的公司
五年前，LUMA Energy 接管了电网。法院的裁决使其合同无效，并给政府一年的时间寻找新的运营商。
波多黎各最高法院裁定，该岛州长可以将这家运营其陷入困境的电网五年的私人公司驱逐出境。这一决定可能会对波多黎各的电力服务产生巨大影响。请听 NPR 的阿德里安·弗洛里多的报道。
阿德里安·弗洛里多连线：2017 年，飓风玛丽亚摧毁了波多黎各本已摇摇欲坠的电网，该岛政府将其私有化。它向一家总部位于加拿大和德克萨斯州、名为 LUMA Energy 的公司提供了一份为期 15 年的接管电力线路的协议，并承诺 LUMA 将重建更强大的电网并改善众所周知的不可靠服务。 LUMA 于 2021 年接手。但事情并没有按计划进行。
停电仍然是生活中常见的事实。 LUMA 受到了客户和官员的严厉批评。去年，州长 Jenniffer Gonzalez-Colon 提起诉讼，要求取消 LUMA 的合同。昨天，波多黎各最高法院做出了对她有利的裁决，LUMA 必须下台。
JENNIFFER GONZALEZ-COLON：今天是岛上庆祝的一天。
弗洛里多：这是州长在裁决后发表的讲话。她说 LUMA 没有兑现其承诺。
冈萨雷斯-科隆：岛上停电更多，岛上停工更多。他们没有履行合同的要求。
佛罗里达州：事实上，该岛最高法院以程序为由作出裁决，称官员在批准与该公司的协议时没有遵循当地要求。法院给了当地政府一年的时间来任命新的运营商。州长表示，寻找新私营公司的工作将立即开始。
冈萨雷斯-科隆：这将是一个很好的过渡。我们将在一年内做到这一点。我希望所有有兴趣参与这一过程的公司都履行并遵守法律程序。我们将开放该流程进行公开招标。

佛罗里达州：法院给 LUMA Energy 10 天的时间要求重新考虑其裁决。 LUMA 在一份声明中表示，正在考虑采取法律选择。该公司长期以来一直辩称，它接管的电网状况很糟糕，停电事件不能完全归咎于它。新的运营商需要得到当地政府和联邦监督委员会的批准，该委员会是国会十年前为帮助波多黎各摆脱破产而设立的。在一份声明中，该董事会批评州长在没有准备好新公司的情况下就终止了 LUMA 的合同。它表示担心岛上服务的连续性。州长在昨天的讲话中表示，她已经制定了计划，并将很快公布。

title_en: Cenk Uygur goes all in on Ro Khanna for 2028
title_zh: Cenk Uygur 全力支持 Ro Khanna 2028 年比赛
summary: Khanna got a "Cenksgiving" surprise on Hasan Piker's stream.
summary_zh: 卡纳在哈桑·派克的直播中收到了“Cenksgiving”惊喜。
body_en: Ro Khanna hasn't launched a 2028 bid yet, but he already has a pioneer of the populist left in his corner.

Progressive firebrand Cenk Uygur is set to formally endorse the California Democrat on Thursday night during his annual appearance on nephew Hasan Piker's Twitch stream, a Thanksgiving Day debate-a-thon the pair call "Cenksgiving." Uygur told POLITICO he will pitch Khanna as the best populist progressive candidate. His Rebellion PAC will also debut its first 2028 ad promoting a Khanna candidacy Thursday night.
"For me, it's a no-brainer," Uygur said in an interview, explaining why he’s backing Khanna. "Who else would you back, and why would any progressive or any populist back anyone else?"

Along with his PAC getting behind Khanna, Uygur is also launching his own "Draft Ro" website to collect signatures and showcase other early high-profile endorsers, though he wouldn't say who just yet.

The endorsement is one of the first of the 2028 cycle, and it comes before any major candidate has formally announced. Inside Washington, Khanna’s chances are viewed as quite slim. But for Uygur, that kind of underestimation is exactly part of the draw.
"I love it," Uygur said of the skepticism. "I wouldn't have backed him if anyone in D.C. was behind him."
"We're running against Washington," he added. "So if Washington doesn't like a candidate, perfect."

Uygur is pairing his endorsement with a litmus test he’s trying to lay down for 2028 progressives: Candidates must call what Israel has done in Gaza a genocide and support ending U.S. funding for Israel. "It isn't actually about Israel," Uygur said. "It's about: Is this person going to represent us or not?"

Khanna, he said, is "among the very, very few, and maybe the only candidate, that'll pass that test." He allowed for one other: "There's also AOC. If she runs, that's another person that could pass the test."

But that's as far as the praise goes. His endorsement of Khanna comes as many other progressives are waiting to see whether Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) jumps in. Uygur isn't one of them. Asked if her entry would change his calculus, he said: "Not 1%."
"Sorry, but I don't think AOC means it," he said. "I don't think she would do any of the things that she says, and so I'm not going to back someone who is not going to deliver."
"She's obsessed with the establishment, so she's going to run a soft, weak race," he added. "She wants to make Democratic leaders and mainstream media happy. Good luck with that strategy."
Khanna has told POLITICO he plans to decide whether to run after the holidays and that whether Ocasio-Cortez gets in won't factor into his decision.

Uygur's backing could give the potential 2028 candidate some credibility on the populist left, not to mention a boost from "The Young Turks," one of the longest-running and most popular progressive shows online, which Uygur launched in 2002. He also co-founded Justice Democrats in 2017 and ran a long-shot bid of his own for the 2024 Democratic presidential nomination. His Rebellion PAC sparked controversy during the 2026 midterms with an ad tying U.S. funding for Israel to higher grocery prices, which the campaign of then-Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed distanced itself from.
Uygur, who was also a prominent backer of Vermont independent Sen. Bernie Sanders' presidential runs, has a blunt prediction for 2028: "I'm positive Ro Khanna is going to win."
body_zh: 罗·卡纳（Ro Khanna）尚未发起 2028 年竞选，但他已经拥有了一位民粹主义先锋。
进步煽动者岑克·维吾尔将于周四晚上在侄子哈桑·派克 (Hasan Piker) 的 Twitch 直播节目中正式支持这位加州民主党人，这场感恩节辩论马拉松被两人称为“Cenksgiving”。维吾尔告诉《政治》杂志，他将把卡纳视为最好的民粹主义进步候选人。他的 Rebellion PAC 也将于周四晚首次推出 2028 年首个广告，宣传卡纳的候选资格。
“对我来说，这是理所当然的，”维古尔在接受采访时说道，并解释了他支持卡纳的原因。 “你还会支持谁，为什么进步主义者或民粹主义者会支持其他人？”
除了政治行动委员会对卡纳的支持外，维吾尔还推出了自己的“Draft Ro”网站，以收集签名并展示其他早期高调的代言人，尽管他尚未透露是谁。
此次认可是 2028 年周期的首批认可之一，而且是在任何主要候选人正式宣布之前进行的。在华盛顿内部，卡纳的机会被认为相当渺茫。但对于维吾尔族来说，这种低估正是吸引力的一部分。
“我喜欢它，”维吾尔谈到怀疑论时说道。 “如果华盛顿有人支持他，我就不会支持他。”
“我们正在对抗华盛顿，”他补充道。 “因此，如果华盛顿不喜欢某个候选人，那就完美了。”
维吾尔将他的支持与他试图为 2028 年进步人士制定的试金石结合起来：候选人必须称以色列在加沙的所作所为是种族灭绝，并支持结束美国对以色列的资助。 “这实际上与以色列无关，”维吾尔说。 “问题在于：这个人是否会代表我们？”
他说，卡纳是“极少数，也许是唯一能够通过这项测试的候选人之一。”他也考虑到了另一个：“还有AOC。如果她参选，那就是另一个可以通过测试的人了。”
但赞美也仅此而已。他对卡纳的支持之际，许多其他进步人士都在观望众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯（纽约州民主党）是否加入。维吾尔人不是其中之一。当被问及她的加入是否会改变他的计算时，他说：“不会改变 1%。”
“抱歉，但我认为 AOC 不是这个意思，”他说。 “我认为她不会做她所说的任何事情，所以我不会支持那些不会兑现承诺的人。”
“她痴迷于当权者，所以她将进行一场软弱的竞选，”他补充道。 “她想让民主党领导人和主流媒体高兴。祝这个策略好运。”
卡纳告诉《政治》杂志，他计划在假期后决定是否参选，奥卡西奥-科尔特斯是否参选不会影响他的决定。

维吾尔人的支持可能会给这位潜在的 2028 年候选人在民粹主义左翼中获得一些可信度，更不用说维吾尔人于 2002 年推出的历史最悠久、最受欢迎的网络进步节目之一《青年土耳其党》的推动。他还在 2017 年共同创办了正义民主党，并以自己的方式竞选 2024 年民主党总统提名。他的叛乱政治行动委员会在 2026 年中期选举期间因一则广告将美国对以色列的资助与更高的杂货价格挂钩而引发争议，当时的参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的竞选团队与这一广告保持了距离。
维吾尔也是佛蒙特州独立参议员伯尼·桑德斯 (Bernie Sanders) 总统竞选的重要支持者，他对 2028 年做出了直率的预测：“我确信罗·卡纳 (Ro Khanna) 将获胜。”

title_en: After Democrats' midterm wins, some hope attacks on DEI will ease
title_zh: 民主党中期选举获胜后，一些人希望对 DEI 的攻击会有所缓解
summary: After the midterms, a Democratic congressman declared that DEI is back. What does Democrats' ascendance portend for diversity initiatives that the Trump administration relentlessly attacked?
summary_zh: 中期选举结束后，一位民主党国会议员宣布 DEI 回来了。民主党的崛起对共和党的多元化倡议预示着什么？
body_en: After Democrats' midterm wins, some hope attacks on DEI will ease After the midterms, a Democratic congressman declared that DEI is back. What does Democrats' ascendance portend for diversity initiatives that the Trump administration relentlessly attacked?
After the midterms, a Democratic congressman declared that DEI is back. What does Democrats' ascendance portend for diversity initiatives that the Trump administration relentlessly attacked?

Since President Trump returned to office, he and his Republican allies have moved aggressively to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion programs across government and the private sector. After Democrats won resoundingly in this month's midterms, California Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna posted this video.
RO KHANNA: Tonight, DEI is back as America celebrated diversity and inclusion.
SUMMERS: So what could the midterms be signaling about the future of DEI? NPR's Adrian Florido reports.

ADRIAN FLORIDO, BYLINE: As a consultant, Lily Zheng helps companies develop programs to improve workplace diversity. Since last year, Zheng has watched most companies retreat from the work, in some cases to do it more quietly and others ending it altogether.
LILY ZHENG: It was fear of retribution. It was fear of political and regulatory pressure.
FLORIDO: But since Democrats prevailed in the midterms, Zheng says there's been a noticeable vibe shift.
ZHENG: Some of my colleagues who have been doing this work with a lower profile have expressed relief, maybe, that now they don't have to be tiptoeing on eggshells, likely.
FLORIDO: It's based on a sense, Zheng says - maybe just a hope - that newly empowered Democrats will find ways to rein in Republican attacks that have had a chilling effect on DEI work.
ANTONIO INGRAM: I think, with this new political landscape, that chilling effect is thawing out.

FLORIDO: Antonio Ingram is an attorney with the NAACP Legal Defense Fund. He says the president's Republican allies in Congress have helped foster a culture of fear around DEI, summoning the leaders of universities, companies and nonprofits to hostile hearings.

INGRAM: To cross-examine them and to intimidate them from continuing to do the work they're doing to create a multiracial democracy. And now we have people who are going to be pro-civil rights in control of those committee hearings.

FLORIDO: But DEI experts that NPR spoke with said institutions are unlikely to quickly jump right back into diversity work, much less promote it publicly. Shaun Harper runs the Race and Equity Center at the University of Southern California. He's hopeful organizations will find their way back to DEI work. But after watching so many retreat from it so quickly, he says...
SHAUN HARPER: I don't expect them to overnight flip on a switch and, you know, declare that DEI is back.

FLORIDO: One reason is that President Trump still controls the federal agencies that have used threats of funding cuts and lawsuits to try to force institutions to end DEI programs. In a statement to NPR, White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster called DEI policies, quote, "racist and destructive." The White House accused President Biden of letting them run rampant and said Trump was elected with a mandate to end these policies. Still, in states that have followed the president's lead on DEI, it seems clear that the midterm Democratic wins could usher in a significant shift, like in Texas.
LILIANA GARCES: That pressure to remove certain readings from your classroom or self-censor is just not going to be as strong.

FLORIDO: Liliana Garces is professor of education at the University of Texas at Austin. She's been studying the impact of state restrictions on DEI programs and race-based curricula. After Republican leaders in Texas banned diversity programs at public universities, she interviewed administrators implementing the bans on their college campuses. And she found that because of the political climate, many feared being accused of not complying.
body_zh: 民主党中期获胜后，一些人希望对 DEI 的攻击会有所缓解 中期选举后，一位民主党国会议员宣布 DEI 又回来了。对于特朗普政府无情攻击的多元化倡议来说，民主党的崛起预示着什么？
中期选举结束后，一位民主党国会议员宣布 DEI 回来了。对于特朗普政府无情攻击的多元化倡议来说，民主党的崛起预示着什么？
自特朗普总统重返办公室以来，他和他的共和党盟友积极采取行动，消除政府和私营部门的多样性、公平和包容性计划。民主党在本月的中期选举中大获全胜后，加州民主党众议员罗·卡纳发布了这段视频。
RO KHANNA：今晚，随着美国庆祝多样性和包容性，DEI 又回来了。
萨默斯：那么中期选举对 DEI 的未来会发出什么信号呢？ NPR 的阿德里安·弗洛里多报道。
阿德里安·弗洛里多连线：作为顾问，莉莉·郑帮助公司制定改善工作场所多样性的计划。自去年以来，郑看到大多数公司都退出了这项工作，有些公司是为了更安静地开展工作，有些公司则干脆结束了这项工作。
郑莉莉：是害怕遭到报复。这是对政治和监管压力的恐惧。
弗洛里多：但自从民主党在中期选举中获胜以来，郑说，气氛发生了明显的转变。
郑：我的一些一直低调从事这项工作的同事可能表示松了一口气，因为他们现在可能不必小心翼翼了。
弗洛里多：郑说，这是基于一种感觉——也许只是一种希望——新获得权力的民主党人会找到方法来遏制共和党的攻击，这些攻击对 DEI 的工作产生了寒蝉效应。
安东尼奥·英格拉姆：我认为，随着新的政治格局的出现，这种寒蝉效应正在消融。
佛罗里达州：安东尼奥·英格拉姆是全国有色人种协进会法律辩护基金的一名律师。他说，总统在国会中的共和党盟友帮助培育了围绕 DEI 的恐惧文化，召集大学、公司和非营利组织的领导人参加充满敌意的听证会。
英格拉姆：盘问他们并恐吓他们继续为创建多种族民主所做的工作。现在我们有支持民权的人来控制这些委员会的听证会。
弗洛里多：但 NPR 采访过的 DEI 专家表示，各机构不太可能迅速重新投入多元化工作，更不用说公开宣传了。肖恩·哈珀 (Shaun Harper) 负责管理南加州大学的种族与公平中心。他希望各组织能够找到恢复 DEI 工作的方式。但在看到这么多人如此迅速地撤退后，他说……
肖恩·哈珀：我不希望他们一夜之间打开开关，然后宣布 DEI 回来了。

弗洛里多：原因之一是特朗普总统仍然控制着联邦机构，这些机构利用削减资金的威胁和诉讼来试图迫使机构终止 DEI 项目。白宫发言人艾莉森·舒斯特 (Allison Schuster) 在给 NPR 的一份声明中称 DEI 的政策是“种族主义和破坏性的”。白宫指责拜登总统任由这些政策猖獗，并表示特朗普当选后有权终止这些政策。尽管如此，在那些在 DEI 上追随总统领导的州，民主党的中期胜利似乎很明显可能会带来重大转变，比如德克萨斯州。
莉莉安娜·加尔斯：从课堂上删除某些读物或进行自我审查的压力不会那么大。
佛罗里达州：莉莉安娜·加塞斯 (Liliana Garces) 是德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的教育学教授。她一直在研究州限制对 DEI 项目和基于种族的课程的影响。在德克萨斯州共和党领导人禁止公立大学多元化项目后，她采访了在大学校园实施禁令的管理人员。她发现，由于政治气候，许多人担心被指控不遵守规定。

title_en: Strobe Talbott, Time magazine reporter and deputy US secretary of state, dies aged 80
title_zh: 《时代》杂志记者、美国副国务卿斯特罗布·塔尔博特去世，享年 80 岁
summary: After 21 years at Time, Talbott joined the Clinton administration and later headed the Brookings Institution Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institut
summary_zh: 在《时代》杂志工作 21 年后，塔尔博特加入了克林顿政府，后来担任布鲁金斯学会的负责人。
body_en: Strobe Talbott, Time magazine reporter and deputy US secretary of state, dies aged 80 | US politics
After 21 years at Time, Talbott joined the Clinton administration and later headed the Brookings Institution
Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.
His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he died peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home.

The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist party of the Soviet Union.
Talbott did, and it landed him a job at the magazine.
After 21 years at Time, where he focused on Soviet-American relations and held positions including Washington bureau chief and a foreign-affairs columnist, he joined the Clinton administration.

Talbott joined the US state department in 1994, swiftly becoming deputy secretary of state. In that role, he was the architect of the administration’s approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the US and India after the latter’s nuclear tests in 1998.

He served as the president of the Brookings Institution, one of the US’s most prominent thinktanks, from 2002 to 2017. In that time, he also chaired the US state department’s foreign affairs policy board.
Talbott authored over a dozen books. His last book was titled Our Founders’ Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump, which was published in 2020.

He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946, and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian; stepdaughter Rebecca Ascher-Walsh; siblings Kirk, Marjo and Page Talbott; and eight grandchildren, according to the New York Times.
His first wife, Brooke Shearer, died in 2009, and he later married author Barbara Lazear Ascher.
body_zh: 《时代》杂志记者、美国副国务卿斯特罗布·塔尔博特去世，享年 80 岁美国政治
在《时代》杂志工作 21 年后，塔尔博特加入克林顿政府，后来担任布鲁金斯学会院长
斯特罗布·塔尔博特（Strobe Talbott）周四去世，他是《时代》杂志的前记者，后来担任比尔·克林顿（Bill Clinton）领导下的副国务卿，后来又担任布鲁金斯学会的负责人。他80岁了。
他的儿子德文·塔尔博特证实，他​​在长期患病后在纽约东汉普顿的家中平静地去世。
老塔尔博特曾在耶鲁大学和牛津大学接受教育，并在那里与克林顿同住。在英国大学期间，在莫斯科《时代》杂志实习后，该杂志要求塔尔博特帮助翻译被泄露的前苏联共产党第一书记尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫的回忆录。
塔尔博特照做了，这让他在杂志社找到了一份工作。
他在《时代》杂志工作了 21 年，专注于苏美关系，并担任过华盛顿分社社长和外交专栏作家等职务，之后加入克林顿政府。
塔尔博特于 1994 年加入美国国务院，很快成为副国务卿。担任该职务期间，他是政府对俄罗斯和其他前苏联国家的政策的设计者，并在 1998 年印度核试验后主持了美国和印度之间的谈判。
2002年至2017年，他担任美国最著名的智库之一布鲁金斯学会主席。期间，他还担任美国国务院外交政策委员会主席。
塔尔博特撰写了十几本书。他的上一本书名为《我们的创始人的警告：理性时代遇见特朗普时代》，于 2020 年出版。
他于 1946 年出生于俄亥俄州代顿，身后有两个儿子：德文 (Devin) 和阿德里安 (Adrian)。继女丽贝卡·阿舍-沃尔什；柯克、玛乔和佩吉·塔尔博特兄弟姐妹；据《纽约时报》报道，他还有八个孙子。
他的第一任妻子布鲁克·希勒 (Brooke Shearer) 于 2009 年去世，后来他与作家芭芭拉·拉泽尔·阿舍尔 (Barbara Lazear Ascher) 结婚。

title_en: U.S. Judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech rights to please Trump
title_zh: 美国法官裁定 FCC 侵犯 ABC 的言论自由权以取悦特朗普
summary: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官阻止特朗普政府审查美国广播公司持有的所有当地广播许可证。该电台在其中六个地区播出
body_en: U.S. Judge: FCC violated ABC’s free speech to please Trump : NPR

U.S. Judge: FCC violated ABC’s free speech to please Trump A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.

Under Chairman Brendan Carr, left, the Federal Communications Commission launched an early review of Disney's licenses to operate all the local ABC stations it owns. New Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro, right, says the company is fighting back to protect ABC's journalistic integrity and free speech. "We're very principled on this," he said. Heather Diehl/Thibault Camus/Pool/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

A federal judge has blocked President Trump and his administration from taking action to challenge the ABC television network's broadcast licenses, finding it to be an unconstitutional punishment for satire, commentary and news coverage that Trump doesn't like.
Disney, ABC battle Trump's FCC in court over free speech protections

In her preliminary injunction filed Wednesday, U.S. District Court Judge Loren AliKhan found that the federal agency's early reviews represented retaliation for speech the Trump administration resented.

Such perceived offenses included late-night host Jimmy Kimmel's jabs at the president, the critical remarks of hosts on the chat show The View , and the moderation of a presidential debate in September 2024.

ABC and its corporate parent, the Walt Disney Co., serve six of the 10 largest markets in the U.S., including New York, Los Angeles, and Houston. They contribute significantly to the network's bottom line.

"Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face -- loss of their broadcast licenses -- the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness," Judge AliKhan wrote.

She rejected the Trump administration's motion to dismiss the lawsuit from ABC and Disney challenging the review of the local licenses. Usually the licenses last eight years and are up for review on a staggered basis. They are rarely taken away.

In her ruling, AliKhan relied heavily on public statements and social media postings in which Trump attacked ABC and Disney, as well as posts by Trump's pick as the chair of the Federal Communications Commission, Brendan Carr.

"What started in 2020 as questions about how ABC 'can keep getting a license' if it 'report[s] fake news,' ... has crescendoed into repeated calls for the Commission to strip ABC's broadcast licenses for their editorial decisions," she wrote. "The court counts eleven such calls made by President Trump over the past two years -- the most recent being in July 2026."
And the judge cited the administration's "tangible steps toward enforcing President Trump and Commissioner Carr's repeated threats to strip the Plaintiff Stations of their licenses."
"Chairman Carr has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders," Judge AliKhan wrote.
Carr did not respond to NPR's request for comment Wednesday evening.
ABC hailed the ruling in a statement as "an important victory for the First Amendment."

Among the targets of ire from Trump and Carr was ABC's decision not to broadcast Trump's July 2026 Oval Office address on its television network. ABC's legal team said the network streamed it on its digital news service, but would not have done so absent the political pressure from the FCC.

It is one of several examples of newsroom decisions made under duress, the network's lawyers said in court. Kimmel's interview with then-Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico of Texas was uploaded to YouTube instead of being aired on ABC's late night television show. (Talarico won election to the U.S. Senate earlier this month.) And The View stopped hosting candidates for political office in 2026 in the months ahead of the fall elections.
body_zh: 美国法官：FCC为了取悦特朗普而侵犯了ABC的言论自由 : NPR
美国法官：FCC为了取悦特朗普而侵犯ABC的言论自由 一名联邦法官阻止特朗普政府审查ABC持有的所有当地广播许可证。这些电台在美国六个最大的市场播出。
在主席布伦丹·卡尔（左）的领导下，联邦通信委员会对迪士尼拥有的所有当地 ABC 电视台的运营许可证进行了早期审查。迪士尼新任首席执行官乔什·达马罗（右）表示，公司正在反击，以保护 ABC 的新闻诚信和言论自由。 “我们对此非常有原则，”他说。 Heather Diehl/Thibault Camus/Pool/法新社来自 Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
一名联邦法官阻止特朗普总统及其政府采取行动挑战美国广播公司电视网络的广播许可证，认为这是对特朗普不喜欢的讽刺、评论和新闻报道的违宪惩罚。
迪士尼和美国广播公司 (ABC) 在法庭上就言论自由保护问题与特朗普的联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 展开斗争
美国地方法院法官洛伦·阿里汗在周三提交的初步禁令中发现，联邦机构的早期审查是对特朗普政府不满的言论的报复。
此类被视为冒犯的行为包括深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔对总统的攻击、主持人在脱口秀节目《The View》中的批评言论，以及对 2024 年 9 月总统辩论的缓和。
ABC 及其母公司华特迪士尼公司为美国 10 个最大市场中的 6 个提供服务，包括纽约、洛杉矶和休斯顿。它们对网络的盈利做出了重大贡献。
法官写道：“鉴于原告可能面临的惩罚的极端性，甚至是生死攸关的性质——失去广播许可证——法院的结论是，过早的许可证续签程序所造成的风险足以让一家普通的广播公司感到不寒而栗。”
她拒绝了特朗普政府驳回美国广播公司和迪士尼对当地许可审查提出质疑的诉讼的动议。通常，许可证的有效期为八年，并且会分阶段接受审查。他们很少被带走。
阿里汗在裁决中严重依赖特朗普攻击美国广播公司和迪士尼的公开声明和社交媒体帖子，以及特朗普任命的联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔的帖子。
她写道：“从 2020 年开始，人们开始质疑 ABC 如果‘报道假新闻’，如何‘能够继续获得许可证’……现在已经逐渐演变成一再呼吁委员会取消 ABC 因其编辑决定而获得的广播许可证。” “法院统计特朗普总统在过去两年中发出了 11 次此类电话——最近一次是在 2026 年 7 月。”
法官还援引了政府“为执行特朗普总统和卡尔专员一再威胁吊销原告电视台执照而采取的切实步骤”。
阿里汗法官写道：“卡尔主席已将特朗普总统的言论作为他的行军命令。”
周三晚上，卡尔没有回应 NPR 的置评请求。
美国广播公司在一份声明中称赞这一裁决是“第一修正案的重要胜利”。
特朗普和卡尔愤怒的目标之一是美国广播公司 (ABC) 决定不在其电视网络上播出特朗普 2026 年 7 月在椭圆形办公室的讲话。美国广播公司的法律团队表示，该网络在其数字新闻服务上播放了该节目，但如果没有联邦通信委员会的政治压力，美国广播公司不会这样做。
该网络的律师在法庭上表示，这是新闻编辑室在胁迫下做出决定的几个例子之一。基梅尔对当时的美国民主党参议员候选人、来自德克萨斯州的詹姆斯·塔拉里科的采访被上传到 YouTube，而不是在美国广播公司的深夜电视节目中播出。 （塔拉里科本月早些时候赢得了美国参议院选举。）在秋季选举前的几个月，The View 停止接待 2026 年政治职务候选人。

title_en: US army calls detonation of bomb chemicals in Iowa a success after fears of toxic plume
title_zh: 由于担心有毒羽流，美国陆军称爱荷华州化学炸弹爆炸成功
summary: The army blows up US stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used for explosives, to avoid uncontrollable explosion The US army blew up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, saying the first checks show Wednesday’s contro
summary_zh: 军队炸毁了美国库存的叠氮化铅（一种用于炸药的化学物质），以避免无法控制的爆炸。
body_en: The army blows up US stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used for explosives, to avoid uncontrollable explosion

The US army blew up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, saying the first checks show Wednesday’s controlled detonation in Iowa didn’t spread toxic dust to nearby homes and farms.

Earthen barriers were put up and foam and water were poured onto a pair of bunkers holding the 5 tons (4,500kg) of lead azide, and officials said those measures appear to have absorbed much of the blast.

The US Environmental Protection Agency air monitors were detecting no lead in the air around the Iowa army ammunition plant in Middletown, and an alert sent to cellphones late Wednesday afternoon said it was safe to resume normal activities. Fema also issued an all clear around the plant, the US army reported.

Still, government agencies and independent researchers plan to do extensive environmental testing for lead – a heavy metal that’s especially dangerous to children and pregnant women – in the weeks ahead on water sources, farms, homes and playgrounds.
The army said the safest option had been detonating the stockpile right away because it was degrading and might explode uncontrollably at any time as the weather got colder.
Some experts cautioned that it’s too early to know whether communities are in the clear.
But Maj Gen Eric Shirley, who led the army operation, said the risk was “reduced as close to zero as it’s absolutely humanly possible”.

Since the military announced and then delayed plans for the detonation over the past two weeks, residents and environmental groups have voiced concerns about potential health and environmental impacts and about a lack of information about what to expect.

An Associated Press reporter filmed the blasts from less than a mile away and upwind from the site. Following two loud booms around 9am local time, a pair of white plumes rolled high in the air before quickly dissipating.
The army attributed the smoke to the foam sprayed on the bunkers to tamp down any dust.
Bystanders who parked on the side of a road to watch came away unimpressed by the size of the explosion.
Burlington resident Tim Brandt said he wanted to feel the ground shake, but instead the detonation reminded him of the noisemakers that crack when thrown on the ground.
“It was nothing,” he told the AP. “It seemed like government put fear in a lot of people over nothing.”

The army scheduled the detonation for Wednesday because the winds were blowing to the south-west and away from populated areas including Burlington, a city of just under 25,000 people along the Mississippi River.
The two controlled blasts destroyed all 68 barrels and didn’t set off any secondary explosions, Shirley said.
Donald Trump posted on social media that the army did a “great job”.
Acting secretary of the army Adam Telle along with the Republican governors of Iowa and Missouri also said it appeared to be a success and that the explosion was well contained.
body_zh: 军队炸毁了美国库存的叠氮化铅（一种用于炸药的化学物质），以避免无法控制的爆炸
美国军方炸毁了该国全部库存的叠氮化铅（一种用于制造炸药的化学物质），并称首次检查显示周三在爱荷华州发生的受控爆炸并未将有毒粉尘传播到附近的房屋和农场。
人们竖起土墙，将泡沫和水倒入两个装有 5 吨（4,500 公斤）叠氮化铅的掩体中，官员们表示，这些措施似乎吸收了大部分爆炸。
美国环境保护署空气监测仪检测到米德尔敦爱荷华州陆军弹药厂周围的空气中没有铅含量，周三下午晚些时候向手机发送的警报称，可以安全地恢复正常活动。据美国军方报道，联邦应急管理局还对工厂周围发布了警报。
尽管如此，政府机构和独立研究人员计划在未来几周内对水源、农场、家庭和游乐场进行广泛的铅环境测试，铅是一种对儿童和孕妇特别危险的重金属。
军方表示，最安全的选择是立即引爆库存，因为它正在退化，并且随着天气变冷，随时可能发生无法控制的爆炸。
一些专家警告说，现在判断社区是否安全还为时过早。
但领导这次军队行动的埃里克·雪利少将表示，风险“已降至接近零，这是人类绝对可能做到的”。
自从军方在过去两周宣布并推迟爆炸计划以来，居民和环保组织对潜在的健康和环境影响以及缺乏有关预期结果的信息表示担忧。
美联社记者在距现场不到一英里的上风处拍摄了爆炸过程。当地时间上午 9 点左右，伴随着两声巨响，一对白色羽状物在空中高高滚滚，然后迅速消散。
军队将烟雾归因于在碉堡上喷洒泡沫以压实灰尘。
路边停车观看的旁观者对爆炸的规模不以为然。
伯灵顿居民蒂姆·布兰特说，他想感受地面的震动，但爆炸却让他想起了扔在地上时发出的噪音。
“这没什么，”他告诉美联社。 “政府似乎无缘无故地让很多人感到恐惧。”
军方定于周三进行爆炸，因为风向是西南风，远离人口稠密地区，其中包括伯灵顿，这座位于密西西比河沿岸、人口不足 25,000 人的城市。
雪莉说，两次受控爆炸摧毁了所有 68 个桶，并且没有引发任何二次爆炸。
唐纳德·特朗普在社交媒体上发帖称，军队做得“很棒”。
代理陆军部长亚当·泰勒以及爱荷华州和密苏里州的共和党州长也表示，这次行动似乎很成功，爆炸得到了很好的控制。

title_en: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
title_zh: 特朗普命令联邦承包商在回应国会之前先与白宫核实
summary: President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就他们从国会收到的询问与他的政府进行磋商
body_en: President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged

NEW YORK -- NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to a new executive order .

The companies must also coordinate with the White House and U.S. agencies on “appropriate responses” to any such requests, the order issued late Friday says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

The order is the Republican administration’s latest effort to resist what are expected to be wide-ranging and aggressive oversight efforts from Democrats when they take over Congress in January. Democrats have made government contracts one of their top investigative targets , noting that federal money has been flowing to companies linked with Trump’s family, particularly at the Pentagon.

White House officials have already begun taking steps to exert more control over how agencies and officials respond to congressional requests, anticipating there will be a flood of investigations initiated by Democrats.

Trump's counsel, Will Scharf, told federal agencies on Monday that they must seek approval from his office and the White House’s Office of Legislative Affairs before agreeing to appear before Congress. Scharf also suggested in a recent letter to Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, that some congressional investigations may amount to “blatant criminality.”

Garcia sent letters this week directing members of Trump’s family and top administration officials to preserve documents. Scharf sought to dismiss the requests, noting in a letter to Democratic lawmakers that they are not yet in the majority and cannot compel compliance.

In a fact sheet , the White House framed the new requirements as “protecting executive privileges from congressional overreach,” arguing that some congressional leaders have tried to intrude on executive branch privileges by “harassing private companies that contract with the federal government.”

Presidents of both parties have long used executive privilege to resist congressional inquiries, but the claims can set up messy, protracted legal fights as parties dispute whether it applies. Executive privilege allows the president to keep information from the courts, Congress and the public to protect the confidentiality of White House deliberations, but the protection is far from absolute.
The latest executive order applies to all contractors and subcontractors, a universe of tens of thousands of businesses.

body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就他们从国会收到的询问与他的政府进行磋商，并保留白宫认为有特权的任何通信
纽约 - 纽约（美联社） - 根据一项新的行政命令，唐纳德·特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就国会提出的质询与他的政府进行磋商，并扣留任何白宫认为特权的通信。
该命令称，这些公司还必须与白宫和美国机构协调，对任何此类请求做出“适当回应”。如果他们不遵守规定，白宫警告他们的合同可能会被终止，并且他们未来与联邦政府的合作可能会暂停。
该命令是共和党政府为抵制民主党在一月份接管国会时预计将采取的广泛而积极的监督措施而采取的最新举措。民主党人已将政府合同作为其首要调查目标之一，并指出联邦资金一直流向与特朗普家族有联系的公司，尤其是五角大楼。
白宫官员已经开始采取措施，对各机构和官员如何回应国会要求施加更多控制，预计民主党将发起大量调查。
特朗普的律师威尔·沙夫周一告诉联邦机构，他们必须获得特朗普办公室和白宫立法事务办公室的批准，然后才能同意出席国会会议。沙夫还在最近给众议院监督委员会民主党领袖、加州众议员罗伯特·加西亚的一封信中表示，一些国会调查可能构成“公然犯罪”。
加西亚本周致函特朗普家族成员和高级政府官员保存文件。沙夫试图驳回这些要求，并在给民主党议员的一封信中指出，他们尚未占多数，无法强迫他们遵守。
