summary: Vice-president says he supports reinstatement of Nvidia CEO after ‘assurances’ from top US officials was ‘under no investigation’ JD Vance said on Wednesday that Jensen Huang , the recently reinstalled Nvidia CEO , was never under criminal investigation and th
summary_zh: JD Vance 周三表示，在美国高级官员“保证”“没有受到调查”之后，副总统表示他支持恢复 Nvidia 首席执行官的职位
body_en: Vice-president says he supports reinstatement of Nvidia CEO after ‘assurances’ from top US officials was ‘under no investigation’

JD Vance said on Wednesday that Jensen Huang , the recently reinstalled Nvidia CEO , was never under criminal investigation and therefore did not need a pardon after Donald Trump said he would be open to offering one to the tech executive.

The vice-president told reporters he supported Huang being reinstated as Nvidia CEO after receiving “assurances” from the attorney general and other top US officials that Huang was “under no investigation”.
“We received the assurances that … he was under no investigation and the accusations against him were based on anonymous reporting, not on actual evidence,” Vance said.
“I don’t think he needs a pardon at all. I haven’t seen any evidence, again, that he committed a crime,” Vance said.
The vice-president’s comments came one day after Trump told the New York Post that it was “always an option” to offer Huang a pardon.
“It’s always an option, I guess,” the president said in interview. “But I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”

Trump and Vance intervened in Nvidia’s leadership drama and put pressure on the tech company’s board to reinstall Huang as the CEO despite other lawmakers’ concerns over whether Huang posed a national security risk for having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia is elite impunity | Moira Donegan
Huang is expected to testify to congressional committees in the coming weeks about Nvidia’s chip exports, Huang’s alleged affair and the US government’s role in having Nvidia reinstate Huang as CEO.

“I think I want [Huang] to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know, a very smart person,” Trump told the New York Post.
Huang has not been formally accused of any crime, and Todd Blanche, the US attorney general, told reporters on Tuesday that no evidence indicated Huang committed a crime.

“To the extent that … the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said.
At the same time, Blanche did not confirm whether the justice department had conducted a thorough investigation into Huang, instead saying law enforcement agents “looked into” the situation.
Yet days earlier, Trump told CNBC that his administration had done “a pretty good investigation” to exonerate Huang.
Vance’s comments appeared to confirm that the DoJ never initiated a formal investigation into Huang.
But lawmakers from both sides of the aisle have questions about the US government’s determination

John Curtis, a Republican who sits on the Senate commerce committee, wrote on X : “Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?”

Pete Ricketts, a Republican who sits on the Senate foreign relations committee, wrote on X on Monday, “Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress. It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips.”
body_zh: 副总统表示，在美国高级官员的“保证”“没有受到调查”之后，他支持恢复英伟达首席执行官的职位
JD 万斯周三表示，最近重新上任的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋从未受到过刑事调查，因此在唐纳德·特朗普表示愿意向这位科技高管提供赦免后，他不需要赦免。
这位副总统告诉记者，在收到司法部长和其他美国高级官员的“保证”，即黄仁勋“没有受到调查”后，他支持黄仁勋恢复担任英伟达首席执行官。
万斯说：“我们得到的保证是……他没有受到调查，对他的指控是基于匿名报告，而不是实际证据。”
“我认为他根本不需要赦免。我再次没有看到任何证据表明他犯了罪，”万斯说。
副总统发表上述言论的一天前，特朗普告诉《纽约邮报》，赦免黄是“永远的一个选择”。
“我想这总是一个选择，”总统在接受采访时说。 “但我认为没有必要。”
特朗普和万斯干预了英伟达的领导层戏剧，并向这家科技公司董事会施压，要求重新任命黄为首席执行官，尽管其他立法者担心黄是否因与所谓的中国间谍有染而构成国家安全风险。
黄仁勋回归英伟达是精英有罪不罚 |莫伊拉·多尼根
预计黄仁勋将在未来几周内向国会委员会作证，内容涉及英伟达的芯片出口、黄仁勋涉嫌的事件以及美国政府在让英伟达恢复黄仁勋首席执行官一职方面所扮演的角色。
“我想我希望[黄]说实话，我的意思是，他的律师将不得不为他提供建议，但我一直发现他是100%光明正大的，而且你知道，他是一个非常聪明的人，”特朗普告诉《纽约邮报》。
黄尚未被正式指控犯有任何罪行，美国司法部长托德·布兰奇周二对记者表示，没有证据表明黄犯有犯罪行为。
布兰奇说：“司法部掌握的信息表明他正在犯罪或类似的事情，也就是说，事实并非如此，如果这是真的，我肯定会告诉总统。”
与此同时，布兰奇没有证实司法部门是否对黄进行了彻底调查，而是表示执法人员正在“调查”情况。
然而几天前，特朗普对 CNBC 表示，他的政府已经进行了“相当不错的调查”，以证明黄无罪。
万斯的言论似乎证实司法部从未对黄发起正式调查。
但两党议员都对美国政府的决心提出质疑
参议院商务委员会的共和党人约翰·柯蒂斯 (John Curtis) 在 X 上写道：“英伟达董事会表示，他们根据美国高级官员的意见得出结论，认为让黄仁勋回来不会构成国家安全风险。我有一些问题。我们政府中的谁参与了权衡？他们告诉了董事会什么？董事会基于什么基础得出不存在风险的结论？”
参议院外交关系委员会成员、共和党人皮特·里基茨 (Pete Ricketts) 周一在 X 上写道，“英伟达今天的决定并不能免除黄仁勋在国会作证的责任。这也不能免除英伟达对国家安全担忧和下落不明的芯片负责的责任。”

summary: Macy’s parade in New York postponed for first time ever as thousands across US north-east face power outages Heavy rain, winds, flooding and high tides crossed holiday plans across the US on Thursday, prompting the cancellations of at least two commercial Than
summary_zh: 纽约梅西百货游行首次推迟，美国东北部数千人面临停电、大雨、大风、洪水和涨潮
body_en: Macy’s parade in New York postponed for first time ever as thousands across US north-east face power outages
Heavy rain, winds, flooding and high tides crossed holiday plans across the US on Thursday, prompting the cancellations of at least two commercial Thanksgiving parades.

A severe winter storm brought foul weather up and down the east coast, causing flooding, widespread power outages and even tornado warnings in several states. On the west coast, record high tides brought coastal flooding to several cities. And winter storm warnings were posted for several parts of the midwest.
On the east coast, all of New Jersey was under a state of emergency, as were parts of New York .

In New York, the traditional Macy’s parade – a fest of vast, inflatable characters – was postponed to Saturday for the first time in its history. One estimate put the cost of re-inflating the balloons with helium at $1.7m. Authorities in Philadelphia ordered that city’s Thanksgiving Day parade, the oldest in the US, off the streets, opting to air it as an “alternative TV event” instead.
More than 900,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday afternoon, with the majority of outages in east coast states.
The storm flooded coastal villages and cities from North Carolina through New Jersey. Roads were closed and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.

Avalon, New Jersey, saw some of the worst flooding in its history, said Scott J Wahl, a local official, adding that several drivers had to be rescued after driving around barricades and into flood waters. The Margate city fire department near Atlantic City, New Jersey, posted a video on Facebook of water pouring through the city’s streets. And residents in flood-prone areas of Atlantic City were strongly urged to voluntarily self-evacuate . “We’d rather be safe than sorry. This is more like a tropical storm than a nor’easter,” said the Atlantic City mayor, Marty Small Sr.
In Norfolk, Virginia, tornado warnings blared on phones around the metro area as families prepared to celebrate Thanksgiving.
South Florida, too, faced a day of constant rain. A tornado brushed the ground in Boynton Gardens in Palm Beach county, 25 miles north of Mar-a-Lago, where Donald Trump is celebrating the holiday.
Meanwhile on the west coast, strong winds and king tides flooded some coastal communities, and demolished part of the famed pier in California’s Pacifica Beach.
Record-breaking California tides cause major flooding of roads and businesses
“King tides” are seasonal high tides, which this year overlapped with a series of factors exacerbating their impact, including unusually high Pacific coast water levels.

Los Angeles and Santa Barbara had tied or broken all-time high tide records on Wednesday, at 8.19 and 8.21ft, respectively, according to the National Weather Service (NWS). La Jolla, California, just north of San Diego, also set an all-time high tide record of 8.11ft (2.5 meters), according to the NWS, while preliminary data suggested that tides in Monterey, south of San Francisco, might also have set an all-time record at 8.03ft .

Flooding risk remained on Thursday. In Marin county, north of San Francisco, officials issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront properties in Stinson Beach, saying large waves expected through the afternoon could send water and debris into roads and homes.
Winter storm warnings and watches were also posted for parts of Missouri and Illinois , with up to 13in of snow expected around St Louis by Thursday afternoon.

Snow fell as far south as north Alabama, where giant flakes dropped from the sky on Thursday morning, although it was just a touch too warm in most locations for it to stick and make it a rare white Thanksgiving.

The weather affected air travel at eastern US airports, with delays expected to last into Friday morning. Adverse aviation conditions included reduced visibility, greater turbulence, strong winds and aircraft icing.
FlightAware reported over 2,200 flights to or from US destinations were delayed and more than 400 were canceled on Thursday. Overall on Wednesday, more than 6,000 flights had been delayed.
body_zh: 纽约梅西百货游行首次推迟，美国东北部数千人面临停电
周四，大雨、大风、洪水和涨潮破坏了美国各地的假期计划，导致至少两次商业感恩节游行被取消。
一场严重的冬季风暴给东海岸带来了恶劣的天气，导致洪水、大范围停电，甚至几个州还发布了龙卷风警报。在西海岸，创纪录的高潮给几个城市带来了沿海洪水。中西部多个地区发布了冬季风暴警报。
在东海岸，新泽西州全境以及纽约部分地区都处于紧急状态。
在纽约，传统的梅西百货游行——一场巨大的充气人物盛宴——历史上首次推迟到周六。据估计，用氦气重新给气球充气的成本为 170 万美元。费城当局下令该市美国最古老的感恩节游行停止在街头举行，而是选择将其作为“另类电视活动”进行播放。
周四下午，超过 90 万户家庭和企业停电，其中东海岸各州大部分停电。
风暴淹没了从北卡罗来纳州到新泽西州的沿海村庄和城市。道路被封闭，紧急救援人员正在从被困水中的汽车中救出人员。

新泽西州阿瓦隆当地官员斯科特·J·瓦尔 (Scott J Wahl) 表示，新泽西州阿瓦隆遭遇了历史上最严重的洪水，并补充说，几名司机在绕过路障并进入洪水后不得不获救。新泽西州大西洋城附近的马盖特市消防局在 Facebook 上发布了一段视频，显示水涌入该市街道。并强烈敦促大西洋城洪水易发地区的居民自愿自行撤离。大西洋城市长马蒂·斯莫尔（Marty Small Sr.）表示：“我们宁愿安全，也不愿后悔。这更像是一场热带风暴，而不是东北风暴。”
在弗吉尼亚州诺福克，当家庭准备庆祝感恩节时，都会区周围的电话响起了龙卷风警报。
南佛罗里达州也面临着持续降雨的一天。一场龙卷风席卷了棕榈滩县博因顿花园的地面，该花园位于海湖庄园以北 25 英里处，唐纳德·特朗普正在那里庆祝节日。
与此同时，在西海岸，强风和大潮淹没了一些沿海社区，并摧毁了加州帕西菲卡海滩著名码头的一部分。
加州破纪录的潮汐导致道路和企业遭受严重洪水
“大潮”是季节性高潮，今年与一系列加剧其影响的因素重叠，包括异常高的太平洋沿岸水位。
据美国国家气象局 (NWS) 称，洛杉矶和圣巴巴拉周三分别追平或打破了历史最高潮汐记录，分别为 8.19 英尺和 8.21 英尺。据国家气象局称，位于圣地亚哥北部的加利福尼亚州拉霍亚也创下了 8.11 英尺（2.5 米）的历史最高潮汐记录，而初步数据表明，旧金山南部蒙特利的潮汐也可能创下了 8.03 英尺的历史最高潮汐记录。
周四洪水风险依然存在。在旧金山北部的马林县，官员向斯廷森海滩海滨房产的居民发出疏散警告，称预计下午的大浪可能会将水和碎片带入道路和房屋。
密苏里州和伊利诺伊州部分地区也发布了冬季风暴警报和预警，预计到周四下午圣路易斯周围降雪量将达到 13 英寸。
周四早上，雪花一直南下到阿拉巴马州北部，巨大的雪花从天而降，尽管大多数地方的天气有点太暖和，无法粘住雪花，使之成为一个罕见的白色感恩节。
天气影响了美国东部机场的航空旅行，预计延误将持续到周五早上。不利的航空条件包括能见度降低、湍流加大、强风和飞机结冰。
FlightAware 报告称，周四有超过 2,200 架往返美国目的地的航班延误，超过 400 架航班被取消。周三共有 6,000 多个航班延误。

title_en: Group of Senate Democrats push to add freshman to leadership
title_zh: 参议院民主党团体推动增加新人担任领导层
summary: Several Democratic senators have been signaling this move, saying the party needs to acknowledge the diverse class of incoming freshman that catapulted the party to victory in November.
summary_zh: 几位民主党参议员一直在暗示这一举措，称该党需要承认即将入学的新生的多元化阶层
body_en: Group of Senate Democrats Several Democratic senators have been signaling this move, saying the party needs to acknowledge the diverse class of incoming freshman that catapulted the party to victory in November.

U.S. Senate Majority Leader Charles Schumer (D-NY), center, is seen here meeting with newly elected Democratic Senators, (L-R) Senator-elect Andy Kim (D-NJ), Senator-elect Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Senator-elect Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) Senator-elect Adam Schiff (D-CA) Senator-elect Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) and Senator-elect Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) at the U.S. Capitol Building on November 12, 2024. That group of senators is pushing to add an incoming freshman senator to the leadership ranks. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images/Getty Images North America hide caption
A group of Senate Democrats elected in 2024 sent a letter to colleagues Tuesday proposing to add an incoming freshman to the leadership ranks.

"The Freshman Representative to Leadership would be elected by members of the incoming freshman class and confirmed by the Conference," the letter said. "We intend to request a vote on this proposal."

The letter, first reported by Politico , is signed by California Sen. Adam Schiff, Maryland Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin, Arizona Sen. Ruben Gallego, Delaware Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, and New Jersey Sen. Andy Kim.
The letter nods to the diverse class of incoming freshmen who helped catapult the party to controlling both chambers of Congress.

"These freshmen have their fingers on the pulse of long-time Democratic voters, those who voted for Democrats for the first time this past Election Day, and everyone in-between," the letter reads. "The deserve a seat at the table."
Senate Democrats have been signaling a desire to uplift new voices in the party.
"On election night, people voted very clearly for a new generation of leadership. That was very, very clear," Slotkin said during remarks at a conference of Democrats after the midterms .
New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker told MS NOW that leadership extends beyond the top post.

"This is a time for new leadership," Booker said, mentioning wanting to see more of incoming Sens. Annie Andrews of South Carolina and James Talarico of Texas. "I want to see them out front, I want to see them taking issues, I want to see them running on the field."
The proposed rule change comes ahead of the leadership election next week. Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer , D-N.Y., for the majority leader.

Senate leadership is comprised not only of the top position of Majority leader but of additional conference officers. Both Van Hollen and Schumer support the idea of adding a position for a freshman to that leadership group.
"Leader Schumer was already planning to do this and is incredibly supportive of the idea," a spokesperson told NPR.

On Tuesday, Van Hollen posted to social media: "There should be a freshman senator on the Senate leadership team. As I've said, we need a new way to organize so we can deliver for the American people."

body_zh: 参议院民主党团体 几位民主党参议员已经发出了这一举动的信号，称该党需要承认不同阶层的新生，正是他们使该党在 11 月取得了胜利。

美国参议院多数党领袖查尔斯·舒默（纽约州民主党）（中）与新当选的民主党参议员会面，从左到右当选参议员安迪·金（新泽西州民主党）、当选参议员鲁本·加列戈（亚利桑那州民主党）、当选参议员安吉拉·阿尔斯布鲁克斯（马里兰州民主党）、当选参议员亚当·希夫（加利福尼亚州民主党）、当选参议员丽莎·布伦特·罗切斯特（德国民主党）和当选参议员2024 年 11 月 12 日，埃丽莎·斯洛特金 (密歇根州民主党议员) 在美国国会大厦。这群参议员正在推动将一位即将上任的新参议员加入领导层。奇普·索莫德维拉/盖蒂图片社/盖蒂图片社北美隐藏标题栏
一群 2024 年当选的参议院民主党人周二致信同事，提议在领导层中增加一名即将上任的新人。
信中说：“新生领导层代表将由新生班成员选举产生，并由大会确认。” “我们打算要求对该提案进行投票。”
这封信最先由 Politico 报道，由加利福尼亚州参议员 Adam Schiff、马里兰州参议员 Angela Alsobrooks、密歇根州参议员 Elissa Slotkin、亚利桑那州参议员 Ruben Gallego、特拉华州参议员 Lisa Blunt Rochester 和新泽西州参议员 Andy Kim 签署。
这封信向不同阶层的新生致敬，他们帮助该党控制了国会两院。
信中写道：“这些新生掌握着长期民主党选民的脉搏，那些在过去的选举日首次投票给民主党的人，以及中间的每个人。” “他们应该在谈判桌上占有一席之地。”
参议院民主党人一直表示希望在党内发出新的声音。
“在选举之夜，人们非常明确地投票支持新一代领导层。这是非常非常明确的，”斯洛特金在中期选举后的民主党会议上发表讲话时表示。
新泽西州参议员科里·布克 (Cory Booker) 告诉《MS NOW》，领导力不仅仅局限于最高职位。
布克说：“这是新领导层的时刻。”他提到希望看到更多即将上任的南卡罗来纳州参议员安妮·安德鲁斯和德克萨斯州参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科。 “我想看到他们在前面，我想看到他们解决问题，我想看到他们在球场上奔跑。”
拟议的规则变更是在下周的领导人选举之前提出的。马里兰州参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 正在挑战参议院少数党领袖、纽约州民主党人查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 的多数党领袖席位。
参议院的领导层不仅由多数党领袖的最高职位组成，还由其他会议官员组成。范霍伦和舒默都支持在该领导小组中增加一个新人职位的想法。
“领导人舒默已经计划这样做，并且非常支持这个想法，”一位发言人告诉 NPR。
周二，范霍伦在社交媒体上发帖称：“参议院领导团队中应该有一名新参议员。正如我所说，我们需要一种新的组织方式，以便我们能够为美国人民做出贡献。”

title_en: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed for 1st time in history
title_zh: 梅西百货感恩节大游行史上首次推迟
summary: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday.
summary_zh: 梅西百货周三表示，梅西百货感恩节游行历史上首次因天气原因推迟。
body_en: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed until Saturday due to weather for first time in its 100-year history - CBS News
For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday.
The 100th annual parade will now kick off Saturday at 8:30 a.m.
The historic move comes as a powerful coastal storm impacted the area Thursday.

"The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our city and agency partners, we've made the decision to move the celebration due to expected severe weather," Macy's said in a statement. "Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday."

"Created by Macy's colleagues since 1924 as a gift to our city and nation, our parade has brought magic into the hearts of millions and have created cherished memories that have spanned generations," Will Coss, executive producer and vice president of Macy's Branded Entertainment, said at a press conference Wednesday . "This year we marked our 100th march, a milestone built on creativity, celebration and tradition. While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our participants and spectators is and always will be our top priority."

"We know that our city is the greatest city in the world, and we also know that in our city, nothing comes easily, and you have to plan for every possibility," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. "And while we were looking forward to celebrating Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow, extreme weather has forced us to reschedule for Saturday instead."
Mamdani pointed to the "heavy storm," with wind gusts up to 65 mph possible, along with flash flooding.

"Now I know many New Yorkers, myself included as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow," Mamdani said. "I know that this change of plan will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first. And on Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker and everyone visiting, will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe."

"By moving the parade to Saturday when weather conditions are much more favorable, we can give New Yorkers the celebration that they've been looking forward to without compromising on safety," NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said.
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul on Wednesday night declared a state of emergency for New York City, along with Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester counties.
"We're expecting heavy rain and strong winds that could create dangerous travel conditions," she wrote on social media.
The watchword for the mayor's office, the NYPD and Macy's is safety, and there's ample reason for concern. Past parades have seen balloons tear, deflate or collide with overhead wires.

In 1997, high winds pushed several balloons out of control. The Cat in the Hat balloon struck a lamppost near Central Park West, which brought down a heavy fixture, injuring four spectators. A woman suffered a fractured skull and coma. Barney and the Pink Panther balloons also ran into trouble and had to be deflated.

In 1993, Sonic the Hedgehog was driven by high winds into a lamppost, injuring spectators and an NYPD officer. Dudley the Dragon hit a lamppost in Columbus Circle in that same parade, ending glass showering down on the crowd.
In 1971, balloons were grounded because of high winds, but even during COVID, the parade went on.

"Our colleagues, our volunteers, our participants - we've spent over two years working on this very parade. This parade has been built with love, with creativity. Since 1924 we've had an opportunity to create memories, to bring joy to millions of people here in New York City. That is our top priority. We're saddened by this shift, but we're optimistic about our opportunity to deliver the most spectacular 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, the best and biggest parade in our history," Coss said. "We look forward to sharing it with all of New York and everyone else across the nation."

The operational challenges involved in shifting the date of the parade are substantial. The parade involves plenty of marching bands and other performers who had been expecting the event on Thursday, and now will need to make alternative arrangements.
Coss said they are in communication with all parade participants, including those who have come from out of state.

"We are optimistic that we're going to be able to maintain the parade that we set out to produce and to deliver to New York City on Thanksgiving," he said. "There's still some logistics to be worked out, but everyone understands what we're up against and is rallying behind us to create the best and most successful 100th parade."
body_zh: 梅西百货感恩节大游行因天气原因推迟至周六举行，这是其 100 年来的首次 - 哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 新闻
梅西百货周三表示，梅西百货感恩节游行历史上首次因天气原因推迟。
第 100 届年度游行将于周六上午 8:30 开始。
这一历史性举动是在周四一场强大的沿海风暴影响该地区之际发生的。
梅西百货在一份声明中表示：“参与者和观众的安全是我们的首要任务，在与我们的城市和机构合作伙伴密切协商后，由于预计的恶劣天气，我们决定推迟庆祝活动。” “感谢成千上万的志愿者、表演者和合作伙伴，他们每年创造了数百万人享受的魔法。我们期待着周六一起庆祝。”

梅西百货品牌娱乐执行制片人兼副总裁威尔·科斯 (Will Coss) 在周三的新闻发布会上表示：“自 1924 年以来，梅西百货的同事们一直在为我们的城市和国家打造礼物，我们的游行给数百万人的心中带来了魔力，并创造了几代人的珍贵回忆。” “今年我们庆祝了游行 100 周年，这是一个建立在创造力、庆祝活动和传统基础上的里程碑。虽然我们对游行被推迟感到心碎，但参与者和观众的安全始终是我们的首要任务。”
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 表示：“我们知道，我们的城市是世界上最伟大的城市，我们也知道，在我们的城市，没有什么是轻而易举的，你必须为每一种可能性做好计划。” “虽然我们期待明天庆祝梅西百货第 100 届感恩节游行，但极端天气迫使我们改在周六举行。”
马姆达尼指出，这场“猛烈风暴”可能会出现时速高达 65 英里/小时的阵风，并伴有山洪暴发。
马姆达尼说：“现在我知道许多纽约人，包括我自己以及世界各地数百万人，都期待着明天举行的游行。” “我知道这个计划的改变会带来不便，但安全必须放在第一位。周六，当气球升上天空时，每个纽约人和每个来访的人都将能够观看一场既真正壮观又安全的表演。”
纽约警察局局长杰西卡·蒂施说：“通过将游行移至天气条件更加有利的周六，我们可以在不影响安全的情况下为纽约人带来他们一直期待的庆祝活动。”
纽约州州长凯西·霍赫尔周三晚间宣布纽约市以及拿骚、萨福克和韦斯特切斯特县进入紧急状态。
她在社交媒体上写道：“我们预计会有大雨和强风，这可能会造成危险的旅行条件。”
市长办公室、纽约市警察局和梅西百货的口号是安全，而且有充分的理由令人担忧。过去的游行中曾出现过气球撕裂、泄气或与架空电线相撞的情况。
1997年，大风使几个气球失控。戴帽子的猫气球撞到了中央公园西附近的一根灯柱，导致一个重型装置落下，导致四名观众受伤。一名妇女头骨骨折并处于昏迷状态。巴尼和粉红豹的气球也遇到了麻烦，不得不放气。
1993年，刺猬索尼克被大风吹到路灯柱上，导致观众和一名纽约警察局官员受伤。在同一次游行中，“龙达德利”撞上了哥伦布圆环的一根灯柱，导致玻璃洒落到人群中。
1971 年，气球因大风而搁浅，但即使在新冠疫情期间，游行仍在继续。
“我们的同事、我们的志愿者、我们的参与者 - 我们为这次游行花了两年多的时间。这次游行是用爱和创造力建造的。自 1924 年以来，我们有机会创造回忆，为纽约市数百万人带来欢乐。这是我们的首要任务。我们对这一转变感到悲伤，但我们对有机会举办最壮观的第 100 届梅西百货感恩节游行、最好、规模最大的游行感到乐观在我们的历史上，”科斯说。 “我们期待与整个纽约和全国其他人分享。”
改变游行日期所涉及的操作挑战是巨大的。游行中有大量行进乐队和其他表演者，他们原本期待周四的活动，但现在需要做出替代安排。
科斯说，他们正在与所有游行参与者保持联系，包括来自州外的人。
他说：“我们乐观地认为，我们将能够维持我们计划在感恩节制作并运送到纽约市的游行。” “还有一些后勤工作需要解决，但每个人都了解我们面临的挑战，并团结在我们身后，打造最好、最成功的第 100 届游行。”

title_en: Father dies while trying to save teen son on icy California mountain hike
title_zh: 父亲在加州冰冷的山地徒步旅行中试图拯救十几岁的儿子时去世
summary: Guillermo Batres was helping his son, who had slid down a hill and was clinging on to a tree, when he lost his footing A 44-year-old man who was trying to help his son navigate an icy patch of a southern California mountain trail slipped and fell roughly 500ft
summary_zh: 吉列尔莫·巴特雷斯 (Guillermo Batres) 正在帮助他从山上滑下来并抓住一棵树的儿子，结果他失去了立足点。 一名 44 岁的男子正在尝试
body_en: Father dies while trying to save teen son on icy California mountain hike | California
Guillermo Batres was helping his son, who had slid down a hill and was clinging on to a tree, when he lost his footing
A 44-year-old man who was trying to help his son navigate an icy patch of a southern California mountain trail slipped and fell roughly 500ft to his death, according to local authorities.

Guillermo Batres, an avid hiker, set off on Sunday morning to summit Mount Baden-Powell in the San Gabriel mountains with his teenage son, according to Steve De Jong, a lieutenant with the Los Angeles county sheriff’s department.
Hiker reunited with backpack 60 years after he fell into a glacier in Austria
Batres recorded a video on Sunday, obtained by the Los Angeles Times, where he panned across the wintry mountain trail, surrounded by green pines. His wife had turned back early into the hike.
In the clip, Batres’s son, Sebastián, could be seen holding trekking poles and smiling faintly beneath his jacket, which was bundled up toward his nose.
The video cut off abruptly as Batres warned his son to be careful in Spanish.
Sebastián had slid down the side of a hill and was clinging on to a tree, De Jong said.
Batres attempted to aid his son, before losing his footing on the ice and falling down the mountain into a gulch.
The Los Angeles county medical examiner’s office determined Batres died from blunt force injuries sustained in an accident.
Two hikers who passed by Sebastián after the deadly fall helped him put spikes on his shoes and get to safety, according to De Jong.
Jennifer Morse, Batres’s niece, wrote in a GoFundMe that their family has been left “shocked, grieving and facing an unimaginable loss”.
body_zh: 父亲在加州冰冷的山地徒步旅行中试图拯救十几岁的儿子时去世加利福尼亚州
吉列尔莫·巴特雷斯（Guillermo Batres）正在帮助他的儿子，他的儿子从山上滑下来，紧紧抓住一棵树，突然失去了立足点
据地方当局称，一名 44 岁男子试图帮助儿子在南加州一条冰冷的山路上行走时不慎从大约 500 英尺高处坠落身亡。
洛杉矶县治安部门中尉史蒂夫·德容 (Steve De Jong) 表示，狂热的徒步旅行者吉列尔莫·巴特雷斯 (Guillermo Batres) 于周日早上出发，带着十几岁的儿子登上圣盖博山脉的贝登堡山 (Mount Baden-Powell)。
奥地利一名徒步旅行者在坠入冰川 60 年后再次与背包重逢
《洛杉矶时报》获得了巴特雷斯周日录制的一段视频，视频中他在寒冷的山路上平移，周围环绕着青松。他的妻子很早就折返去徒步旅行了。
在视频中，可以看到巴特雷斯的儿子塞巴斯蒂安拿着登山杖，在他的夹克下面微笑着，夹克一直包到他的鼻子上。
当巴特雷斯用西班牙语警告他的儿子要小心时，视频突然中断。
德容说，塞巴斯蒂安从山坡上滑了下来，紧紧抓住一棵树。
巴特雷斯试图帮助他的儿子，但他在冰上失去了立足点，从山上掉进了峡谷。
洛杉矶县法医办公室确定巴特雷斯死于事故中的钝器伤。
德容说，在塞巴斯蒂安摔倒后，两名徒步旅行者路过塞巴斯蒂安身边，帮助他在鞋子上钉上钉子，并帮助他安全抵达安全地带。
巴特雷斯的侄女詹妮弗·莫尔斯 (Jennifer Morse) 在 GoFundMe 上写道，他们的家人“感到震惊、悲伤，面临着难以想象的损失”。

title_en: ‘These families will be essentially homeless’: Flatbush groups condemn response to building collapse
title_zh: “这些家庭基本上将无家可归”：弗拉特布什团体谴责对建筑物倒塌的反应
summary: Advocacy groups say displaced families were sent to ‘subpar hotels’ until 30 November, with no housing plans in place afterward Flatbush community leaders are in an uproar on behalf of those who have been displaced in the aftermath of an apartment building col
summary_zh: 倡导组织表示，流离失所的家庭在 11 月 30 日之前都被送往“劣质酒店”，在弗拉特布什社区租赁之后没有制定住房计划
body_en: Advocacy groups say displaced families were sent to ‘subpar hotels’ until 30 November, with no housing plans in place afterward

F latbush community leaders are in an uproar on behalf of those who have been displaced in the aftermath of an apartment building collapse in Brooklyn earlier this month. They say some displaced tenants are in hotels until 30 November, but have no housing plans after that date.

Advocacy groups said that those who were displaced were sent to “subpar hotels” that were also home to roaches and mice. Stays were only set for up to four days, leaving community leaders to push for longer stays.
Several residents were also sent to hotels in Manhattan over an hour away from their communities in Brooklyn via public transit.
“It is a ticking timebomb until there are actual solutions,” said the Mutual Aid for Flatbush, a nonprofit coalition in the neighborhood where the building fell.

The coalition said they’ve been working with families from all three residential buildings affected by the wreckage, raising about $131,000 through donations from community residents. The funds are being distributed to the families affected by the collapse.
“There is complete disorganization and lack of transparency with the displaced tenants,” a spokesperson for the coalition said in a statement.
Brooklyn building collapse kills at least two children and six adults, injuring 18

The 11 November building collapse stemmed from a weakened foundation as a result of an excavation at a construction site directly next to the apartment, according to the New York Times . The collapse at 1321 Flatbush Avenue killed eight people, left 18 injured and exposed a wall in the building that was attached to 1323 Flatbush. Evacuation orders for 1323 and 1327 Flatbush were issued for all residents in those buildings.

New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the day after the collapse that the American Red Cross set up a supply center at the Flatbush YMCA down the street from the wreckage. The YMCA provided temporary housing, social services and mental health support. It was also announced that the mayor’s office was working with the Department of Buildings on the wreckage recovery efforts.
But the support center only operated for less than a week.
“Our hearts remain with the friends, families, and neighbors whose lives were forever changed by the tragic building collapse,” the Red Cross said in a statement to the Guardian.

City officials said $60,000 was distributed to the impacted residents and families through gift cards for urgent needs during their recoveries, according to the New York Times . Flatbush residents say about $3,000 was on each gift card, and the Flatbush Development Corporation (FDC) also provided $200 gift cards to families, but it’s unclear how many were given out.

Additionally, hotel prices in New York City have greatly fluctuated over the last week given that the holidays are a prime season for tourism. Some estimates note that the average hotel price in the five boroughs were more than $300 a night, meaning a $3,000 gift card would cover housing for a displaced resident for roughly 10 days or less.

The mayor’s office reported in a statement on social media that they’re helping cover the costs for funerals, connecting immigrants with legal aid, working with the health department and the FDC, and are accepting donations for further support for victims.
“It seems as though right now it is a toss-up of responsibility across multiple people,” the coalition said.
The buildings department did not respond for comment.
Many of the impacted residents were undocumented immigrants, making matters more difficult for relocation and rehabilitation efforts.
“A lot of the resources that these families are being told they will get do not apply to them yet because of their paperwork situation,” Mutual Aid said.
body_zh: 倡导组织表示，流离失所的家庭在 11 月 30 日之前都被送往“劣质酒店”，此后没有任何住房计划
本月早些时候，在布鲁克林一栋公寓楼倒塌事件中，弗拉特布什社区领导人为那些流离失所的人们表示了愤怒。他们表示，一些流离失所的租户在 11 月 30 日之前都会住在酒店，但在那之后就没有住房计划了。
倡导团体表示，那些流离失所的人被送往“劣质酒店”，那里也是蟑螂和老鼠的家园。停留时间只设定为最多四天，因此社区领导人不得不推动延长停留时间。
一些居民还被送往曼哈顿的酒店，乘坐公共交通距离布鲁克林的社区有一个多小时的路程。
“在找到真正的解决方案之前，这就像一颗定时炸弹，”大楼倒塌附近的非营利联盟弗拉特布什互助组织 (Mutual Aid for Flatbush) 表示。
该联盟表示，他们一直在与受残骸影响的所有三栋住宅楼的家庭合作，通过社区居民的捐款筹集了约 131,000 美元。这些资金正在分发给受倒塌影响的家庭。
该联盟发言人在一份声明中表示：“流离失所的租户完全混乱且缺乏透明度。”
布鲁克林大楼倒塌造成至少两名儿童和六名成人死亡，18 人受伤
据《纽约时报》报道，11 月 11 日的大楼倒塌是由于公寓旁边的建筑工地进行挖掘导致地基削弱所致。弗拉特布什大道 1321 号的倒塌事故导致 8 人死亡、18 人受伤，并暴露了与弗拉特布什大道 1323 号相连的建筑物的一堵墙。 1323 号和 1327 号弗拉特布什大楼的所有居民都收到了疏散令。
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 在倒塌事故发生后的第二天宣布，美国红十字会在废墟附近的弗拉特布什基督教青年会 (Flatbush YMCA) 设立了一个供应中心。基督教青年会提供临时住房、社会服务和心理健康支持。另据宣布，市长办公室正在与建筑部合作开展残骸打捞工作。
但该支持中心只运营了不到一周。
红十字会在给《卫报》的一份声明中表示：“我们的心与朋友、家人和邻居同在，他们的生活因悲剧性的建筑倒塌而永远改变。”
据《纽约时报》报道，市政府官员表示，已通过礼品卡向受影响的居民和家庭发放了 6 万美元，以满足他们康复期间的紧急需求。弗拉特布什居民表示，每张礼品卡的金额约为 3,000 美元，弗拉特布什发展公司 (FDC) 还向家庭提供了 200 美元的礼品卡，但不清楚发放了多少张。
此外，由于假期是旅游旺季，纽约市的酒店价格在上周波动较大。据估计，这五个行政区的酒店平均价格超过每晚 300 美元，这意味着一张 3,000 美元的礼品卡可以为流离失所的居民提供大约 10 天或更短的住宿费用。
市长办公室在社交媒体上发表声明称，他们正在帮助支付葬礼费用，为移民提供法律援助，与卫生部门和自由民主党合作，并接受捐款以进一步支持受害者。
该联盟表示：“现在看来，这是多人责任的争夺。”
屋宇署没有回应置评。
许多受影响的居民是无证移民，这使得搬迁和重建工作变得更加困难。
互助组织表示：“由于文书工作的原因，这些家庭被告知将获得的许多资源并不适用于他们。”

The turkey's been carved, the pie's been gobbled up and the family squabbles have been (mostly) settled. Now comes Black Friday, the unofficial kickoff to the holiday shopping season.
While many stores open early to jump-start their holiday sales, some services may have limited hours on the Friday after Thanksgiving.
Read on for a snapshot of which stores are open and their hours, as well as any services that may operate differently on Black Friday.
Some stores extend their hours on Black Friday, with many consumers planning to kick off their holiday shopping.
One major exception is outdoor retailer REI, which earlier this month said it would give its 12,000 employees the day off on Black Friday.

Markets reopen on Friday after being closed for Thanksgiving. But investors should be aware that the stock market will close early at 1 p.m. on Black Friday.
Most major banks are open on the day after Thanksgiving because it is not a Federal Reserve holiday or a federal holiday.
Yes, the U.S. Postal Service will be open on the day after Thanksgiving because it is not a federal holiday. Regular mail delivery will resume Friday, Nov. 27, according to the USPS .

title_en: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
title_zh: 朝鲜金正恩无视特朗普的提议后誓言要制造更多核武器
summary: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.
summary_zh: 据报道，领导人金正恩视察了生产核原料的设施，并呼吁建造更多核武器以应对来自世界各地的威胁。
body_en: In this photo provided by the North Korean government, leader Kim Jong Un inspects a facility the government says is for producing weapons-grade nuclear material at an undisclosed location in North Korea, Monday, Nov. 25, 2026. Korean Central News Agency/Korea News Service via AP hide caption
Korean Central News Agency/Korea News Service via AP

SEOUL, South Korea — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring U.S. President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia.
Experts say Kim likely wants to show off his evolving nuclear arsenal, the backbone of his authoritarian rule, and reaffirm his rejection of any future talks on dismantling his nuclear program.

The North's official Korean Central News Agency said Thursday that Kim inspected two nuclear materials production factories, one newly inaugurated and the other being expanded. KCNA photos showed Kim and senior military officials walking between dense rows of what appeared to be centrifuges used to produce weapons-grade uranium and touring halls displaying what were believed to be warheads. Some of the images were blurred.
KCNA said Kim visited a nuclear-powered equipment production base and a nuclear research institute as well on Wednesday.

North Korea has disclosed a uranium enrichment site a few times since it showed one at its main Yongbyon nuclear complex to visiting American scholars in 2010. North Korea didn't say where the nuclear materials production factories that Kim visited this week are located. In June, when North Korea disclosed parts of a uranium enrichment site while reporting on Kim's visit there, outside experts assessed it was likely an additional uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon.

Kim justifies nuke program by citing threats from US, South Korea Kim said his latest inspection visit was part of efforts to strengthen North Korea's defense capabilities in response to "variable nuclear threats approaching the Korean Peninsula moment by moment." He accused the U.S. of inciting its regional allies to possess nuclear-powered submarines and committing to sharing its nuclear weapons with them, KCNA said.

"The validity and substantiality of our possession of nuclear weapons and the trend of bolstering up its nuclear capability in quality and quantity are an irreversible reality," Kim said, according to KCNA.

Kim also said the deployment of low-yield battlefield nuclear weapons across multiple domains for various missions is crucial and urgent given North Korea's "inevitable reality facing the border with the most dangerous enemy state," a reference to South Korea. North Korea has in recent years focused on developing such tactical nuclear weapons amid heightened animosity with South Korea.

"Trump has talked about a willingness to meet Kim Jong Un, but the basic U.S. position that North Korea must denuclearize remains unchanged. So Kim Jong Un wants to say 'Look at how powerful we are. Don't talk about denuclearization if you want to meet us,'" said Moon Seong Mook, an analyst for the Seoul-based Korea Research Institute for National Strategy.

Moon said Kim's visit to the nuclear facilities was also likely meant to check on how state objectives on the nuclear program have progressed this year and what future goals must be set ahead of a year-end Workers' Party conference.

South Korea's Defense Ministry said it takes Kim's comments on battlefield nuclear weapons seriously and added that Seoul maintains a firm military readiness against Pyongyang's nuclear threats under an alliance with the U.S. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff declined to share an analysis of the North Korean nuclear facilities reported by KCNA, calling it confidential information for South Korea and the U.S.

Trump still hopes to meet Kim Trump reiterated his eagerness to restore diplomacy with Kim as he visited China last week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. But a Trump-Kim meeting didn't happen, with Pyongyang not publicly responding to Trump's overture.

In an interview with the New York Post this week, Trump dismissed the suggestion that Kim had rebuffed his outreach, saying, "No, he didn't ignore it. You know, we had many leaders there … There'll be a time when we meet … It was just not really the right time. It was a very busy two-day period."

Trump also claimed he could revive diplomacy with Kim at any time by restarting the exchange of letters they maintained during his first term, although he acknowledged that the two leaders had not corresponded "recently."

Kim has previously said he could return to talks if the U.S. drops its "hostile policy" against his country and respects what he calls the North's status as a nuclear state. Experts say Kim aims to win international recognition as a nuclear state so that he could demand the lifting of international sanctions.

Last week, International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi assessed North Korea has been expanding its original uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, calling the move "a cause for serious concern."

Nuclear weapons can be built using either highly enriched uranium or weapons-grade plutonium, and North Korea has facilities to produce both at Yongbyon. Last year, South Korea's Unification Minister Chung Dong-young said that North Korea was operating four uranium enrichment facilities and that they were running every day.
body_zh: 在朝鲜政府提供的这张照片中，领导人金正恩于 2026 年 11 月 25 日星期一在朝鲜的一个秘密地点检查了政府所说的用于生产武器级核材料的设施。朝鲜中央通讯社/韩国新闻社通过美联社隐藏标题栏
朝鲜中央通讯社/韩国新闻社（美联社）
韩国首尔——朝鲜领导人金正恩视察了生产核原料的设施，并呼吁制造更多核武器，几天前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在最近访问亚洲期间提出了会面的提议。
专家表示，金正恩可能想炫耀他不断发展的核武库，这是他独裁统治的支柱，并重申他拒绝未来任何有关废除核计划的谈判。
朝鲜官方通讯社朝中社周四称，金正恩视察了两家核材料生产工厂，一家是新落成的，另一家正在扩建。朝中社的照片显示，金正恩和高级军事官员在密集的一排似乎是用于生产武器级铀的离心机和展示据信是弹头的参观大厅之间行走。一些图像变得模糊。
朝中社称，金正恩周三还参观了核动力设备生产基地和核研究所。
自2010年向来访的美国学者展示其主要宁边核设施的铀浓缩设施以来，朝鲜已多次披露了铀浓缩设施。朝鲜没有透露金正恩本周访问的核材料生产工厂位于何处。 6月，当朝鲜在报道金正恩访问那里时披露了铀浓缩设施的部分内容时，外部专家评估这可能是宁边的另一个铀浓缩设施。
金正恩以来自美国和韩国的威胁为核计划辩护 金正恩表示，他最近的视察是加强朝鲜防御能力的努力的一部分，以应对“时时刻刻逼近朝鲜半岛的各种核威胁”。朝中社称，他指责美国煽动其地区盟友拥有核动力潜艇，并承诺与它们分享核武器。
据朝中社报道，金正恩表示：“我们拥有核武器的有效性和实质性以及在质量和数量上增强核能力的趋势是不可逆转的现实。”
金正恩还表示，鉴于朝鲜“不可避免地面临与最危险敌国边境的现实”（指的是韩国），在多个领域部署低当量战场核武器以执行各种任务至关重要且紧迫。近年来，在与韩国的敌意加剧的情况下，朝鲜一直致力于发展此类战术核武器。
“特朗普已经谈到愿意与金正恩会面，但美国关于朝鲜必须无核化的基本立场没有改变。所以金正恩想说，‘看看我们有多强大。如果你想见我们，就不要谈论无核化，’”首尔韩国国家战略研究院分析师文成穆(Moon Seong Mook)表示。
文在寅表示，金正恩访问核设施也可能是为了检查今年国家核计划目标的进展情况，以及在年底劳动党会议之前必须制定哪些未来目标。
韩国国防部表示，认真对待金正恩关于战场核武器的评论，并补充说，首尔在与美国结盟的情况下，对平壤的核威胁保持坚定的军事准备状态。韩国参谋长联席会议拒绝分享朝中社报道的朝鲜核设施的分析，称其为韩国和美国的机密信息。
特朗普仍希望与金正恩会面 特朗普上周访问中国参加亚太经合组织峰会时重申了他与金正恩恢复外交的渴望。但特金会并没有发生，平壤也没有公开回应特朗普的提议。
在本周接受《纽约邮报》采访时，特朗普驳斥了有关金正恩拒绝与他接触的说法，他说：“不，他并没有忽视这一点。你知道，我们那里有很多领导人……我们会有一个会面的时间……只是时机不太合适。那是非常忙碌的两天。”
特朗普还声称，他可以随时恢复与金正恩的外交关系，恢复他们在第一个任期内保持的信函往来，尽管他承认两位领导人“最近”没有进行过通信。
金正恩此前曾表示，如果美国放弃对朝鲜的“敌对政策”并尊重他所说的朝鲜核国家地位，他可能会重返会谈。专家表示，金正恩的目标是赢得国际社会对核国家的承认，以便他可以要求取消国际制裁。
上周，国际原子能机构总干事拉斐尔·格罗西评估朝鲜一直在扩建其位于宁边的原始铀浓缩设施，称此举“引起严重关切”。
核武器可以使用高浓缩铀或武器级钚来制造，朝鲜在宁边拥有生产这两种材料的设施。去年，韩国统一部长官郑东泳表示，朝鲜正在运营四个铀浓缩设施，而且它们每天都在运行。

President Trump on Thursday downplayed the importance of Russia and China's intelligence sharing with Iran amid reports that Tehran's allies have helped it target U.S. military bases.

Mr. Trump, during a short press conference with reporters at his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, noted that the Iran conflict had been discussed during his recent trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"My meeting with President Xi was an incredible meeting. I think that they're very little involved with Iran. They could get involved, but involvement to me would mean shooting, not giving them little information," Mr. Trump said.
He added: "We do the same thing, by the way. And you know, when they say that they may be spying on us, well, we spy on them too."
Regarding Russia's intelligence sharing, Mr. Trump said, "I don't think they give very much."
He said both countries want to see the conflict with Iran end.
"I think they're helping me in that regard," Mr. Trump said.
Days after the Iran war broke out, multiple sources, including a senior U.S. official, told CBS News that Russia was providing intelligence to Iran regarding U.S. positions in the Middle East.

官方媒体周四报道称，沙特阿拉伯南部吉赞地区一家炼油厂遭到袭击，造成一人死亡，并导致部分工厂暂时关闭，而几小时前，首次报道该设施遭到袭击。
沙特通讯社援引能源部的话称，“袭击造成一名尼泊尔工人死亡，另有几名不同国籍的工人受伤”，并补充说袭击引发了火灾。
此次袭击发生之前，伊朗支持的胡塞武装声称周三对沙特阿拉伯首都金融区以及该国东部一座庞大的炼油厂发动了袭击。
2026 年 11 月 26 日下午 3:00 德国逮捕了 2 名涉嫌与伊朗相关恐怖组织有关联的伊拉克人
德国当局周四以涉嫌恐怖主义罪逮捕了两名伊拉克男子。据称，这些嫌疑人是与伊朗有关的恐怖组织的成员，据称该组织的目标是美国、以色列和欧洲的犹太机构。

title_en: Rescuers blocked from a fire. A child killed on the way to school. Miles-long trains are upending US lives
title_zh: 救援人员被火势挡住。一名儿童在上学途中被杀。数英里长的火车正在颠覆美国人的生活
summary: Communities say big railroad companies won’t act and that lawmakers are moving too slowly to address a major problem The drive from the Lockland fire station to a house fire on Patterson Avenue should have taken no more than 45 seconds . But East Wyoming Avenu
summary_zh: 社区表示大型铁路公司不会采取行动，立法者在解决重大问题上行动太慢洛克兰火灾统计数据的推动力
body_en: Communities say big railroad companies won’t act and that lawmakers are moving too slowly to address a major problem
The drive from the Lockland fire station to a house fire on Patterson Avenue should have taken no more than 45 seconds .

But East Wyoming Avenue and Davis Street were both blocked: a Norfolk Southern train was stopped across several streets – the fire engine had to turn around and take a detour via a nearby highway. By the time firefighters snaked through the highway traffic and reached the fire last month, seven minutes after the call came in, 89-year-old Marian Haefner was dead in her own home .
“We lost a house here about five years ago, on Central Avenue which is directly on the other side of the tracks. Same thing, couldn’t get to it,” says Mark Mason, Lockland’s mayor.
“I’ve been mayor of Lockland for nine years. Frankly, [Norfolk Southern] don’t give a crap. If they did, they would do something about it.”

From his office in a century-old building in Lockland, a small community north of Cincinnati, Mason reels off a list of complaints about train crossing blockages he’s been fielding: People threatened with dismissal because they are constantly late to work. Parents paying extra to daycares because they’re late picking up their children. College students who have had to drop out of a class because they can’t get to campus on time.

Lockland is several miles south of the Sharonville intermodal terminal, a link of the Heartland Corridor that links an Atlantic seaport in Norfolk, Virginia, with Chicago. It is from this terminal that Norfolk Southern trains are moved on to the tracks across Lockland streets, sometimes for up to 23 hours, to make room for other trains to be connected, say local officials.

“I’ve had it. It’s 2026 – trains should not be affecting people’s lives like this, much less putting them in danger. It’s an easy fix – quit pulling out trains if they can’t move forward [but train companies] are a powerful entity,” Mason says.
Rail companies own most tracks and lines in the US. Local and state authorities have scant ability to regulate.
Lockland is far from alone in dealing with Norfolk Southern, a $73bn public company with a long line of environmental and other charges against it.
Similar rail crossing incidents have been happening in Cleveland , Chicago , Houston and beyond.

In Hammond, Indiana a 2023 Pro Publica investigation found children regularly having to climb through cars to get to and from school. Local administrators say Norfolk Southern backed out of building a pedestrian overpass.

Over the past 12 months there have been more than 34,000 public reports of rail crossing blockages, according to the Federal Railroad Administration, a sharp increase from more than 25,000 reports over the previous 12 months. Texas alone made up almost 10,000 of those, with Ohio seeing the third-highest number of reports in that time.

In almost a quarter of those incidents, pedestrians crawling on, over or between rail cars were reported. In nearly 22%, first responders were unable to cross the tracks. Numerous other reports found students at the University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa having to climb through stopped cars to get to campus.
In 2023, Houston reported 5,610 reports of blocked rail crossings, with the city’s East End reporting the highest number of complaints in the country, according to local reports.
Last December, Sylvia Garcia, a Texas congresswoman whose district includes the East End, reintroduced a bill prohibiting trains from blocking rail crossings for more than 10 minutes.

“We tragically lost 15-year-old Sergio Rodriguez , who was killed by an oncoming train while trying to get to Milby high school. No child should have to risk their life getting to school, and no family should have to worry about a blocked train delaying emergency care. Our communities deserve better,” she says.

“Republicans have allowed this legislation to languish in committee while powerful railroad companies continue putting their bottom lines ahead of the safety of our communities. These companies have spent years making promises while our families continue paying the price.”

Ohioans have had a troubled relationship with Norfolk Southern in recent years. In February 2023, a failed wheel bearing caused a train derailment and catastrophic chemical fire in East Palestine. The company settledwith the justice department and Environmental Protection Agency for more than $310m.
body_zh: 社区表示大型铁路公司不会采取行动，立法者在解决重大问题上行动太慢
从洛克兰消防局开车到帕特森大道发生火灾的房屋应该不会超过 45 秒。
但东怀俄明大道和戴维斯街均被封锁：一列诺福克南方火车在几条街道上被拦住，消防车不得不掉头绕道附近的高速公路。上个月，接到电话七分钟后，当消防队员蜿蜒穿过高速公路交通到达火场时，89 岁的玛丽安·海夫纳 (Marian Haefner) 已死在自己的家中。
“大约五年前，我们在中央大街失去了一栋房子，就在铁轨的另一边。同样的情况，我们无法到达，”洛克兰市长马克·梅森说。
“我担任洛克兰市市长已有九年了。坦率地说，[诺福克南方]根本不在乎。如果他们这么做，他们会采取一些措施。”
梅森在位于辛辛那提北部小社区洛克兰的一栋百年建筑内的办公室里，滔滔不绝地列出了他一直在处理的一系列有关火车道口堵塞的投诉：人们因为经常上班迟到而受到解雇威胁。父母因为接孩子迟到而向日托中心支付额外费用。由于无法按时到达校园而不得不退学的大学生。
洛克兰位于沙伦维尔联运码头以南几英里处，该码头是连接弗吉尼亚州诺福克大西洋海港和芝加哥的中心地带走廊的一环。当地官员表示，诺福克南方铁路的火车就是从这个终点站转移到洛克兰街道对面的铁轨上，有时长达 23 小时，以便为其他火车腾出空间。
“我已经受够了。现在是 2026 年了，火车不应该像这样影响人们的生活，更不用说让他们处于危险之中。解决办法很简单，如果火车无法前进，就不再拉动它们（但火车公司）是一个强大的实体，”梅森说。
铁路公司拥有美国大部分轨道和线路。地方和州当局缺乏监管能力。
洛克兰并不是唯一一家与诺福克南方公司打交道的公司，这家市值 730 亿美元的上市公司面临着一系列环境和其他指控。
类似的铁路交叉口事件在克利夫兰、芝加哥、休斯顿等地也发生过。
在印第安纳州哈蒙德，Pro Publica 2023 年的一项调查发现，孩子们经常需要爬汽车上下学。当地管理人员表示，诺福克南方铁路公司放弃了修建人行天桥的计划。
根据联邦铁路管理局的数据，过去 12 个月内，已有超过 34,000 份有关铁路道口堵塞的公开报告，较前 12 个月的 25,000 多份报告大幅增加。仅德克萨斯州就占了近 10,000 起，俄亥俄州的报告数量当时排名第三。
据报道，在这些事件中，近四分之一是行人在火车车厢上、上方或之间爬行。近 22% 的急救人员无法穿越铁轨。许多其他报告发现，塔斯卡卢萨阿拉巴马大学的学生必须爬过停着的汽车才能到达校园。
据当地报道，2023 年，休斯顿报告了 5,610 起铁路道口堵塞的报告，其中该市东区的投诉数量为全国最多。
去年12月，德克萨斯州女议员西尔维娅·加西亚（Sylvia Garcia）的选区包括东区，重新提出一项法案，禁止火车阻塞铁路道口超过10分钟。
“我们不幸失去了 15 岁的塞尔吉奥·罗德里格斯 (Sergio Rodriguez)，他在试图前往米尔比 (Milby) 高中时被迎面驶来的火车撞死。任何孩子都不应该冒着生命危险去上学，任何家庭也不应该担心火车受阻而延误紧急护理。我们的社区值得更好，”她说。
“共和党人允许这项立法在委员会中搁置，而强大的铁路公司继续将自己的底线置于我们社区的安全之上。这些公司花了数年时间做出承诺，而我们的家庭却继续付出代价。”
近年来，俄亥俄州与诺福克南方航空的关系一直存在问题。 2023 年 2 月，车轮轴承故障导致东巴勒斯坦发生火车脱轨和灾难性化学火灾。该公司与司法部和环境保护局达成和解，赔偿金额超过 3.1 亿美元。

title_en: Republican wants FBI and CIA answers before questioning Nvidia chief
title_zh: 共和党人希望联邦调查局和中央情报局在质询英伟达首席执行官之前得到答案
summary: "The public is rightly concerned," says the Republican lawmaker, who wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats and whether Jensen Huang was warned.
summary_zh: 这位共和党议员表示：“公众的担忧是正确的。”他想知道联邦调查局和中央情报局对潜在的国家安全威胁了解多少
body_en: GOP lawmaker seeks answers over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang : NPR

GOP lawmaker seeks answers over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang "The public is rightly concerned," says the Republican lawmaker, who wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats and whether Jensen Huang was warned.
Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Penn., on Nvidia CEO's upcoming House committee interview
Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., speaks at a House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing in Washington on Sept. 21, 2022. Samuel Corum/Getty Images hide caption
Lawmakers seek answers on the national security as Nvidia CEO returns
Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia with President Trump's backing. But the questions surrounding the AI chipmaker and its ties to China are far from settled.

U.S. intelligence officials told congressional staff there is no evidence that Alice Huang, the woman who had an affair with the Nvidia chief, was a Chinese spy or intelligence asset, according to a person familiar with the matter who was granted anonymity to speak about a closed-door briefing.

There is also no evidence that she initiated the affair to collect intelligence for China's government, the person told NPR's Ryan Lucas on condition of anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the matter. She is, however, believed to have passed along information after the affair began.

Trump has said he helped arrange Huang's return as CEO, and Nvidia's board maintains that his reinstatement presents no national security risk. Some Republican lawmakers, however, want to understand how those conclusions were reached.

Speaking to Morning Edition on Wednesday, before NPR obtained the new information, Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., said he wants to hear from the FBI and CIA before Huang appears before House lawmakers next week.

For Fitzpatrick, a former FBI special agent who sits on the House Intelligence Committee, the inquiry begins with what federal authorities knew and whether they warned the Nvidia chief of potential espionage threats.
"What briefings did they give? When did they give them?" he asked.
Huang's reinstatement, Fitzpatrick said, should not put those questions to rest.
"The public is rightly concerned, and they deserve answers," he said.

Fitzpatrick also wants to hear from Attorney General Todd Blanche, who on Tuesday described Nvidia as a good corporate citizen, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department faces questions over Nvidia's chip exports to China.
"Anytime you do an investigation, you follow the facts wherever they lead, and you report those facts with unimpeachable integrity," Fitzpatrick said. "You leave no stone unturned."
The debate over Huang's reinstatement extends beyond Washington.
In Silicon Valley, his return has alarmed women and advocates who have spent years pushing for a better workplace culture, renewing questions about the limits of executive accountability.

body_zh: 共和党议员寻求英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的答案：NPR
共和党议员寻求英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的答案 这位共和党议员表示，“公众的担忧是正确的”，他想知道联邦调查局和中央情报局对潜在的国家安全威胁了解多少，以及黄仁勋是否受到警告。
宾夕法尼亚州共和党众议员布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克 (Brian Fitzpatrick) 接受 Nvidia 首席执行官即将接受的众议院委员会采访
宾夕法尼亚州共和党众议员布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克 (Brian Fitzpatrick) 于 2022 年 9 月 21 日在华盛顿举行的众议院外交事务小组委员会听证会上发表讲话。塞缪尔·科鲁姆/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
英伟达首席执行官回归后，立法者寻求国家安全问题的答案
在特朗普总统的支持下，黄仁勋重新执掌英伟达。但围绕这家人工智能芯片制造商及其与中国的关系的问题还远未解决。
据一位不愿透露姓名的知情人士透露，美国情报官员告诉国会工作人员，没有证据表明与英伟达首席执行官有染的女性爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是中国间谍或情报人员。
该人士对美国国家公共广播电台的瑞安·卢卡斯表示，也没有证据表明她发起了这起事件是为了为中国政府收集情报。由于此事敏感，该人士要求匿名。然而，据信她在事件开始后就传递了信息。
特朗普表示，他帮助安排了黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官，而英伟达董事会坚称，他的复职不会带来国家安全风险。然而，一些共和党议员想了解这些结论是如何得出的。
周三，在 NPR 获得新信息之前，宾夕法尼亚州共和党众议员布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克 (Brian Fitzpatrick) 表示，他希望在黄下周出现在众议院议员面前之前听取联邦调查局 (FBI) 和中央情报局 (CIA) 的意见。
对于担任众议院情报委员会成员的前联邦调查局特工菲茨帕特里克来说，调查始于联邦当局所知道的情况以及他们是否警告过英伟达负责人潜在的间谍威胁。
“他们做了什么简报？他们什么时候做的？”他问道。
菲茨帕特里克说，黄的复职不应消除这些问题。
“公众的担忧是正确的，他们应该得到答案，”他说。
菲茨帕特里克还希望听取司法部长托德·布兰奇（Todd Blanche）和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克（Howard Lutnick）的意见，前者周二将英伟达描述为良好的企业公民，后者的部门面临英伟达向中国出口芯片的质疑。
菲茨帕特里克说：“无论何时进行调查，你都会遵循事实，无论事实如何，并以无可挑剔的诚信报告这些事实。” “你不遗余力。”
关于黄的复职的争论超出了华盛顿范围。
在硅谷，他的回归引起了女性和倡导者的警惕，她们多年来一直在推动更好的工作场所文化，并重新提出了关于高管问责制局限性的问题。

title_en: Powerful Thanksgiving Day storm causes flooding, power outages
title_zh: 强大的感恩节风暴导致洪水、停电
summary: The storm hammered sections of the East Coast with torrential rain, high winds and flooding, knocking out power to hundreds of thousands of customers.
summary_zh: 风暴袭击了东海岸部分地区，带来暴雨、大风和洪水，导致数十万客户停电。
body_en: A Thanksgiving storm brought foul weather to the East Coast and Midwest on Thursday, causing major power outages, disrupting holiday travel and prompting the historic postponement of New York City's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

More than 900,000 customers were without power Thursday evening across the Midwest and Northeast, according to the utility tracking website PowerOutage.us. Of those, more than 200,000 customers were without electricity in Pennsylvania, along with more than 100,000 in each of Virginia and Missouri.
By Thursday evening, more than 2,000 flights to or from U.S. destinations had been delayed and more than 420 were canceled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.

The storm hammered sections of the East Coast with torrential rain, high winds and flooding. All of New Jersey was under a state of emergency , declared by Gov. Mikie Sherrill on Wednesday night, as were parts of New York , following a declaration from Gov. Kathy Hochul. The weather service posted wind advisories from northern Georgia to most of the mid-Atlantic to southern New England.
Stormy weather creates havoc in New York City

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday morning that two people had to be rescued from their cars because of flooding. He cautioned people not to attempt to walk, bike or drive through flooded areas.
"We want to remind everyone to stay safe and there is no destination worth your safety," Mamdani said.

The New York City Emergency Management agency reported that the city received 1.5 to 2 inches of rain on Thanksgiving, with some parts seeing up to 3 inches. High tides brought flooding to the city's coastal areas, including portions of Staten Island and Long Island.
Central Park saw wind gusts higher than 30 mph, the agency said, while LaGuardia Airport recorded winds of 56 mph.
Macy's postponed the annual Thanksgiving parade until Saturday because of concerns about how the parade's massive balloons would fare in the wind-swept canyons between Manhattan's skyscrapers.
A high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, near Houston, said it raised a staggering $350,000 to allow its 500 members to stay in New York City for two extra nights.

"This was quite a challenge for us, and there was a very frantic and large call to action to our community to let the kids stay here and finish it out," Ryan Demkovich, the director of the Pride of Pearland Marching Band for Pearland High School, told CBS News on Thursday.

Visitors who had traveled to New York to attend the parade were forced to make last-minute changes to their travel plans. Amanda Anderson, a Florida-based makeup artist who was hired to do makeup for parade performers, told CBS News New York she was able to rebook her flights so she could stay an extra day.

"I was in Macy's, actually, when I found out, and I look up and there was like three girls crying already," Anderson said when she learned the parade had been postponed. "People were sitting down, very somber. It was an experience."
Major roadways flooded, holiday travel disrupted

The storm flooded coastal villages and cities from North Carolina through New Jersey as the high tide rolled in Thursday morning. Roads were closed and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.
Avalon, New Jersey, was seeing some of the worst flooding in its history, Borough of Avalon Business Administrator Scott J. Wahl said.
"Not quite Hurricane Sandy," Wahl said of the benchmark storm for his village on the far south of New Jersey's Atlantic coast.
Floodwaters washed debris over the road next to the shore, and a few drivers had to be rescued after driving around barricades and into floodwaters, but no injuries were reported, Wahl said.

Lance Miller, 54, said floods in his neighborhood of Ocean City, a small coastal town in New Jersey, are about a foot deep and that driving to the nearest grocery store would probably "destroy your car."
body_zh: 周四，一场感恩节风暴给东海岸和中西部带来恶劣天气，导致严重停电，扰乱了假日旅行，并促使纽约市梅西百货感恩节游行历史性推迟。
据公用事业跟踪网站 PowerOutage.us 称，周四晚上，中西部和东北部地区有超过 90 万客户停电。其中，宾夕法尼亚州有超过 20 万用户断电，弗吉尼亚州和密苏里州各有超过 10 万用户断电。
根据航班跟踪服务 FlightAware 的数据，截至周四晚间，已有 2,000 多个往返美国目的地的航班延误，420 多个航班被取消。
风暴袭击了东海岸部分地区，带来暴雨、大风和洪水。周三晚上，州长米基·谢里尔宣布新泽西州全境进入紧急状态，继州长凯西·霍赫尔宣布纽约部分地区进入紧急状态。气象部门发布了从乔治亚州北部到大西洋中部大部分地区到新英格兰南部的风力警告。
暴风雨天气给纽约市造成严重破坏
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼周四上午表示，由于洪水，必须从车内救出两人。他警告人们不要试图步行、骑自行车或开车穿过洪水地区。
马姆达尼说：“我们想提醒大家注意安全，没有任何目的地值得您的安全。”
纽约市应急管理机构报告称，感恩节该市降雨量为 1.5 至 2 英寸，部分地区降雨量高达 3 英寸。涨潮给该市沿海地区带来洪水，包括史泰登岛和长岛的部分地区。
该机构表示，中央公园的阵风时速超过 30 英里/小时，拉瓜迪亚机场的风速达到 56 英里/小时。
梅西百货将一年一度的感恩节游行推迟到周六，因为担心游行的巨型气球在曼哈顿摩天大楼之间的狂风峡谷中如何飞行。
来自休斯顿附近德克萨斯州皮尔兰的一个高中游行乐队表示，他们筹集了 35 万美元，让其 500 名成员能够在纽约市多住两晚。
“这对我们来说是一个相当大的挑战，我们的社区强烈呼吁采取行动，让孩子们留在这里完成这一切，”皮尔兰高中“皮尔兰骄傲”游行乐队的指挥瑞安·德姆科维奇周四告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻。
前往纽约参加游行的游客被迫在最后一刻改变他们的旅行计划。佛罗里达州的化妆师阿曼达·安德森 (Amanda Anderson) 受聘为游行表演者化妆，她告诉纽约哥伦比亚广播公司新闻 (CBS News New York)，她可以重新预订航班，这样她就可以多待一天。
“事实上，当我发现这一消息时，我正在梅西百货，我抬头一看，已经有三个女孩在哭了，”安德森在得知游行被推迟时说道。 “人们坐下来，非常忧郁。这是一次经历。”
主要道路被淹，假期出行受阻
周四早上涨潮时，风暴淹没了从北卡罗来纳州到新泽西州的沿海村庄和城市。道路被封闭，紧急救援人员正在从被困水中的汽车中救出人员。
阿瓦隆行政区商业管理员斯科特·J·瓦尔 (Scott J. Wahl) 表示，新泽西州阿瓦隆遭遇了历史上最严重的洪水。
“不完全是飓风桑迪，”瓦尔在谈到新泽西州大西洋海岸最南端村庄的基准风暴时说道。
瓦尔说，洪水冲刷了岸边道路上的碎片，一些司机在绕过路障进入洪水后不得不获救，但没有人员伤亡的报告。
54 岁的兰斯·米勒 (Lance Miller) 表示，他所在的新泽西州沿海小镇大洋城附近的洪水大约有一英尺深，开车去最近的杂货店可能会“毁掉你的车”。

Storm Postpones Thanksgiving Day Parade, Trump's New Tariffs, Iowa Post-Detonation

Severe storms sweeping across the nation threaten to cause widespread travel delays today , as millions of people gather with their loved ones. New York City officials announced that the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been rescheduled to Saturday due to the threat of powerful wind gusts that could reach up to 60 mph. This year marked the 100th procession, and the first time the iconic event is being postponed.

Workers inflate the Spider-Man balloon during Macy's Balloon Inflation 2026 on November 25, 2026 in New York City. Macy's plans to celebrate its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade with a record 100 inflatables, but forecasted high winds are threatening to ground the giant balloons. Adam Gray/Getty Images hide caption

🎧 Something is happening across almost every part of the country right now , NPR's Kat Lonsdorf tells Up First . Extreme high tides are affecting the West Coast, snow is expected in parts of the Midwest, and in the South and Southeast, a major storm is advancing up the East Coast. Meteorologist Richard Bann with the National Weather Service Weather Prediction Center tells Lonsdorf the East Coast storm is the primary concern . Bann says the storm will become better organized throughout the day, bringing strong winds and heavy rain that could lead to coastal flooding. The good news: Forecasters expect the East Coast's major storm to move on, mostly wrapping up by Saturday, Lonsdorf says.

The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs targeting goods from 14 major U.S. trading partners , including China, Japan and the European Union. Administration officials argue the measures counter unfair foreign trade practices, though critics question their ultimate effectiveness. Proposed rates may reach 40% on Chinese imports, 35% on Vietnamese goods, and 20-25% on products from other targeted nations. Additional tariffs on Brazilian sugar and aircraft are also being suggested.

🎧 U.S. Trade Ambassador Jamieson Greer said that new tariffs could take effect within a couple of months. For each country, the White House has listed a "proposed" rate and a "deal" rate, NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben says. For example, if talks with China progress positively, they may receive a deal rate of 20%, which is different from its proposed rate of 40%. Although the Supreme Court overturned President Trump's previous tariffs, the new ones fall under Section 301 , a law meant to counter unfair trade practices. The administration says these countries exhibit "structural excess capacity" in various manufactured goods, a situation caused by policies that lead to overproduction, which can distort the global market.

Federal scientists are testing the air, soil and water in Eastern Iowa for lead contamination after the U.S. Army detonated thousands of pounds of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown yesterday. Officials said the controlled explosion was the only safe way to dispose of the bomb-making compound.

🎧 Eliza Billingham of NPR network station Iowa Public Radio says the major concern is the potential release of lead into the air from the explosion. She adds that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has tested the area since the detonation and hasn't found lead in the air. The EPA has deployed around 300 people to sample the air, ground and nearby water. Lead is a neurotoxin that especially endangers children and pregnant people because it can impede childhood development. After a week and a half of delays and inconsistent communication from the Army, residents have grown hesitant about the Army and the EPA's initial findings, Billingham says. Residents want independent monitoring and the University of Iowa and the University of Illinois are conducting regional sampling. Results are expected in a few days and should show if their measurements align with the EPA's data, Billingham says.

A federal judge has blocked Trump from challenging the ABC television network's broadcast licenses. U.S. District Court Judge Loren AliKhan ruled that the president retaliating against satire and commentary he dislikes is unconstitutional. AliKhan issued the preliminary injunction yesterday and dismissed the administration's request to throw out ABC and Disney's lawsuit challenging the review of the local license . Licenses typically last eight years and are rarely revoked. AliKhan's decision drew heavily on Trump's public statements and social media posts against ABC and Disney, as well as comments from Brendan Carr, the president's pick for chair of the Federal Communications Commission.
Our brains are wired to seek out newness, and the retail industry is set up to keep us coming back for more as quickly as possible. J Studios/Getty Images hide caption

Holiday shopping season is in full swing. Before you spend, consider if you actually need what's in your cart. Sales are exciting because our brains are wired to seek newness. Retailers capitalize on that urge. To escape the cycle of constantly wanting more, shop intentionally and appreciate what you already own, says Eric Athas, author of Saying No to New . He shares his insights on breaking this cycle and finding joy in your current possessions with Life Kit .
🛒 Delete the app or remove your credit card info if you have one-click checkout with a company.
🛒 Add an item to your online shopping cart and leave it for 24 hours. Research shows that delaying a purchase decreases your interest in it.
🛒 Make intentional choices. Don't reject all new things. After you understand this, you can learn to say no to the wrong items and yes to the right ones.
🛒 Revisiting old things can provide you with untapped enjoyment in them, research has found. You can apply this by rereading a book or by traveling to a city you have visited before.

风暴推迟了感恩节游行、特朗普的新关税、爱荷华州爆炸后
今天，席卷全国的强风暴可能会导致大范围的旅行延误，数百万人与亲人相聚。纽约市官员宣布，由于时速可能达到 60 英里的强阵风威胁，梅西百货感恩节大游行已改期至周六举行。今年是第 100 届游行，也是这一标志性活动首次被推迟。
2026 年 11 月 25 日，纽约市，工人们在 2026 年梅西百货气球充气活动期间为蜘蛛侠气球充气。梅西百货计划用创纪录的 100 个充气气球来庆祝其第 100 届感恩节游行，但预计大风可能会使巨型气球停飞。亚当·格雷/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏

NPR 的 Kat Lonsdorf 告诉 Up First，现在全国几乎每个地方都在发生一些事情。极端涨潮正在影响西海岸，中西部部分地区预计会下雪，而在南部和东南部，一场大风暴正在向东海岸推进。国家气象局天气预报中心的气象学家理查德·班恩告诉朗斯多夫，东海岸风暴是首要关注的问题。班恩表示，风暴将在全天变得更加有组织，带来强风和大雨，可能导致沿海洪水。好消息：朗斯多夫说，预报员预计东海岸的大风暴将继续下去，大部分在周六结束。
特朗普政府提议对来自中国、日本和欧盟等美国 14 个主要贸易伙伴的商品征收新关税。政府官员认为这些措施旨在打击不公平的外贸行为，但批评者质疑其最终效果。拟议的对中国进口商品征收的关税可能达到 40%，对越南商品征收 35%，对来自其他目标国家的产品征收 20-25%。还建议对巴西糖和飞机征收额外关税。

🎧 美国贸易大使贾米森·格里尔表示，新关税可能会在几个月内生效。 NPR 的丹妮尔·库茨莱本 (Danielle Kurtzleben) 表示，对于每个国家，白宫都列出了“提议”利率和“交易”利率。例如，如果与中国的谈判取得积极进展，他们可能会获得20%的交易率，这与提议的40%不同。尽管最高法院推翻了特朗普总统之前的关税，但新关税属于旨在打击不公平贸易行为的第 301 条法律的管辖范围。美国政府表示，这些国家在各种制成品方面表现出“结构性产能过剩”，这是由导致生产过剩的政策造成的，这可能会扭曲全球市场。
美国陆军昨天在米德尔敦的爱荷华州陆军弹药厂引爆了数千磅不稳定的叠氮化铅后，联邦科学家正在测试爱荷华州东部的空气、土壤和水的铅污染情况。官员们表示，受控爆炸是处理炸弹制造化合物的唯一安全方法。

🎧 NPR 网络电台爱荷华州公共广播电台的 Eliza Billingham 表示，主要担心的是爆炸可能导致铅释放到空气中。她补充说，自爆炸以来，美国环境保护局已经对该地区进行了测试，没有在空气中发现铅。 EPA 已部署约 300 人对空气、地面和附近的水进行采样。铅是一种神经毒素，特别危害儿童和孕妇，因为它会阻碍儿童发育。比林厄姆说，经过一周半的延误和陆军的沟通不一致，居民对陆军和环保局的初步调查结果越来越犹豫。居民希望进行独立监测，爱荷华大学和伊利诺伊大学正在进行区域抽样。比林厄姆说，预计几天后就会得出结果，并且应该显示他们的测量结果是否与美国环保局的数据相符。

一名联邦法官阻止特朗普质疑美国广播公司电视网络的广播许可证。美国地方法院法官洛伦·阿里汗裁定，总统对他不喜欢的讽刺和评论进行报复是违宪的。阿里汗昨天发布了初步禁令，并驳回了政府的要求，即驳回美国广播公司和迪士尼对当地许可证审查提出质疑的诉讼。许可证的有效期通常为八年，很少被撤销。阿里汗的决定在很大程度上参考了特朗普针对美国广播公司和迪士尼的公开声明和社交媒体帖子，以及总统提名的联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔的评论。
我们的大脑天生就喜欢寻找新鲜事物，而零售业的建立就是为了让我们尽快回来购买更多东西。 J Studios/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
假日购物季正如火如荼地进行。在消费之前，请考虑您是否确实需要购物车中的商品。销售令人兴奋，因为我们的大脑天生就喜欢寻求新鲜事物。零售商利用了这种冲动。 《对新事物说不》一书的作者埃里克·阿萨斯说，为了摆脱不断想要更多的循环，有意识地购物并欣赏你已经拥有的东西。他通过 Life Kit 分享了他关于打破这个循环并在当前拥有的东西中找到快乐的见解。
🛒 如果您与公司进行一键结账，请删除该应用程序或删除您的信用卡信息。
🛒 将商品添加到您的在线购物车并保留 24 小时。研究表明，延迟购买会降低您的兴趣。
🛒 做出有意的选择。不要拒绝一切新事物。了解这一点后，您可以学会对错误的项目说“不”，对正确的项目说“是”。
🛒 研究发现，重温旧事物可以给你带来前所未有的乐趣。您可以通过重读一本书或去您以前访问过的城市旅行来应用这一点。
